topics.title: Scatterplots and models of best fit

questions.stem: What is the value of $-7-(-12)$?
questions.solution: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its opposite: $-7-(-12)=-7+12$. Starting at $-7$ and moving $12$ units up the number line gives $5$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-3)(-4)(-2)$?
questions.solution: Multiply two factors at a time. $(-3)(-4)=12$ because a negative times a negative is positive. Then $12\times(-2)=-24$. Three negative factors leave an odd count of negatives, so the product is negative.

distractors.B: added the three numbers instead of multiplying: $-3-4-2=-9$
distractors.C: added the magnitudes and kept the result positive: $3+4+2=9$
distractors.D: assumed every pair of negatives cancels, so the product came out positive

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-5)^2$?
questions.solution: The brackets put the negative sign inside the base, so the whole of $-5$ is squared: $(-5)^2=(-5)(-5)=25$. A negative times a negative is positive.

distractors.A: applied the exponent before the sign, as though the expression were $-5^2=-(5\times 5)=-25$
distractors.B: multiplied the base by the exponent and kept the sign: $-5\times 2=-10$
distractors.C: multiplied the base by the exponent: $5\times 2=10$

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-36}{-4}$?
questions.solution: A negative divided by a negative is positive. Dividing the magnitudes, $36\div 4=9$, so $\dfrac{-36}{-4}=9$.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $-3(x-5)$?
questions.solution: Multiply $-3$ by each term inside the brackets. $-3\cdot x=-3x$ and $-3\cdot(-5)=+15$, since a negative times a negative is positive. The result is $-3x+15$.

distractors.A: multiplied $-3$ by $5$ instead of by $-5$, missing the sign on the second term
distractors.B: multiplied only the first term and copied $-5$ unchanged
distractors.D: distributed $3$ rather than $-3$, dropping the leading negative sign

questions.stem: What is the value of $4-(-6)-(-1)$?
questions.solution: Each subtraction of a negative becomes an addition: $4-(-6)-(-1)=4+6+1$. Adding gives $11$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $9-(-4)$?
questions.solution: Subtracting a negative adds its opposite: $9-(-4)=9+4=13$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-15-(-6)$?
questions.solution: $-15-(-6)=-15+6$. Starting at $-15$ and moving $6$ units toward zero gives $-9$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $12-(-5)+(-3)$?

distractors.A: read both brackets as subtraction, computing $12-5-3$
distractors.B: turned $-(-5)$ into $-5$ and $+(-3)$ into $+3$, computing $12-5+3$
distractors.D: made every term positive and computed $12+5+3$

questions.stem: What is the value of $-8+(-3)-(-11)$?
What is the value of $-6-(-6)+(-4)$?

distractors.A: read both brackets as subtraction, computing $-6-6-4$
distractors.D: flipped both signs the same way, computing $-6+6+4$

questions.stem: At 6 a.m. the temperature was $-9$ degrees Fahrenheit. By noon it had risen $14$ degrees. What was the temperature at noon, in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.solution: A rise of $14$ from $-9$ gives $-9+14=5$ degrees.

distractors.A: added the two sizes and kept the negative sign, giving $-(9+14)$
distractors.B: computed $14-9$ correctly but copied the sign of the starting value
distractors.D: ignored the negative sign and added $9+14$

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-4)(-7)$?
questions.solution: Two negative factors give a positive product, so $(-4)(-7)=28$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-48}{6}$?
questions.solution: One negative and one positive give a negative quotient: $\dfrac{-48}{6}=-8$.

questions.stem: Which of the following products is negative?
questions.solution: A product is negative exactly when it has an odd number of negative factors. Choice B has three negative factors, so $(-1)(-2)(3)(-4)=-24$. The others have four, two and two.

distractors.A: counted four negative signs and assumed more negatives means a negative product
distractors.C: saw two negative signs and expected the product to stay negative
distractors.D: believed any product built from negative numbers is negative

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-2)(-3)(-4)$?
questions.solution: $(-2)(-3)=6$, then $6(-4)=-24$. Three negative factors give a negative product.

distractors.B: added the factors instead of multiplying, computing $-2-3-4$
distractors.C: stopped after multiplying the first two factors
distractors.D: treated the negatives as cancelling out and left the product positive

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-5\cdot 6}{-3}$?
questions.solution: The numerator is $-5\cdot 6=-30$, and $\dfrac{-30}{-3}=10$ because a negative divided by a negative is positive.

questions.stem: The product of two numbers is $-36$. One of the numbers is $-4$. What is the other number?
questions.solution: The missing number is $\dfrac{-36}{-4}=9$. Check: $(-4)(9)=-36$.

distractors.A: subtracted instead of dividing, computing $-36-(-4)$
distractors.B: assumed a negative product must come from a negative partner
distractors.D: added instead of dividing, computing $36+4$

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-3)^3$?
questions.solution: The whole of $-3$ is cubed: $(-3)(-3)(-3)=9(-3)=-27$. An odd power of a negative number is negative.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-4^2$?
questions.solution: With no bracket, the exponent applies only to $4$: $-4^2=-(4^2)=-16$.

distractors.B: multiplied the base by the exponent, computing $-4\cdot 2$
distractors.C: multiplied the base by the exponent and dropped the sign
distractors.D: treated the expression as $(-4)^2$ and squared the negative as well

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-2)^5$?
questions.solution: $(-2)^5$ multiplies five copies of $-2$. Five negative factors is an odd count, so the result is negative: $-32$.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions has a negative value?
questions.solution: $-5^2$ means $-(5^2)=-25$. The others are $16$, $9$ and $25$, all positive, because an even power of a negative number is positive.

distractors.A: assumed a negative base gives a negative value at any exponent
distractors.B: assumed the negative sign inside the bracket survives the squaring
distractors.D: overlooked that the bracket makes the whole of $-5$ the base

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $-2(x+7)$?
questions.solution: Multiply both terms by $-2$: $-2\cdot x=-2x$ and $-2\cdot 7=-14$, giving $-2x-14$.

distractors.A: multiplied only the first term by $-2$ and copied the $7$
distractors.B: used negative times positive equals positive on the second term
distractors.D: dropped the negative sign from the first term

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $-(3x-8)$?
questions.solution: A leading minus multiplies every term by $-1$: $-3x$ and $-(-8)=+8$, giving $-3x+8$.

distractors.B: changed the sign of the first term only
distractors.C: removed the bracket without changing any sign
distractors.D: changed the sign of the second term only

questions.stem: The expression $-5(2x-3)$ can be written in the form $ax+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. What is the value of $b$?
Which expression is equivalent to $-4(x-2y+3)$?
questions.solution: Multiply each of the three terms by $-4$: $-4x$, $-4(-2y)=+8y$, and $-4(3)=-12$.

distractors.A: multiplied only the first term and copied the other two
distractors.B: kept the middle term negative instead of flipping its sign
distractors.C: flipped the middle sign but also flipped the last term to $+12$

questions.stem: What is the value of $-3+5(-2)$?
What is the value of $5-3(-4)$?
questions.solution: Multiply before subtracting: $3(-4)=-12$, so the expression is $5-(-12)=5+12=17$.

distractors.A: subtracted before multiplying, computing $(5-3)(-4)$
distractors.B: treated $-3(-4)$ as $-12$ and computed $5-12$
distractors.C: subtracted before multiplying and dropped the negative sign

questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\dfrac{-7}{2}$?
questions.solution: A single negative sign can sit in front of the fraction, on the numerator, or on the denominator without changing the value, so $\dfrac{-7}{2}=-\dfrac{7}{2}$.

distractors.A: dropped the negative sign when moving it out of the fraction
distractors.C: moved the sign to the denominator while leaving it on the numerator, creating two negatives
distractors.D: added a second negative sign, which returns the value to positive

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-4}{-10}$?
questions.solution: A negative divided by a negative is positive, and $\dfrac{4}{10}=0.4$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-2)^4-\left(-2^4\right)$?
questions.solution: In $(-2)^4$ the brackets make $-2$ the base, so $(-2)^4=16$. In $-2^4$ only $2$ is raised to the power and the sign is applied afterwards, so $-2^4=-16$. Then $16-(-16)=16+16=32$.

distractors.A: kept the negative sign on the fourth power, taking $(-2)^4=-16$ and $-2^4=+16$, giving $-16-16=-32$
distractors.B: treated the two expressions as having the same value, so their difference came out as $0$
distractors.C: replaced $-2^4$ with $-2\times 4=-8$, giving $16-(-8)=24$

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2-3x$. What is the value of $f(-4)$?
Which expression is equivalent to $(x-7)(x+3)$?
questions.solution: Multiply every pair of terms: $x\cdot x=x^2$, $x\cdot 3=3x$, $-7\cdot x=-7x$ and $-7\cdot 3=-21$. The two middle terms give $3x-7x=-4x$, so the product is $x^2-4x-21$.

distractors.A: treated both constants as negative, giving a middle term of $-7x-3x=-10x$
distractors.C: multiplied $-7$ by $3$ as though both were negative, giving $+21$
distractors.D: reversed the sign of the middle term, adding $7x-3x=4x$ instead of $3x-7x$

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-5(-3)^2}{-9}$?
questions.solution: Work out the power first: $(-3)^2=9$. The numerator is $-5\cdot 9=-45$. Then $\dfrac{-45}{-9}=5$, since a negative divided by a negative is positive.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-4-2(3-7)$?
questions.solution: Work inside the brackets first: $3-7=-4$. Then $-2(-4)=+8$, so the expression is $-4+8=4$.

distractors.A: ignored the brackets and read the expression as $-4-2\cdot 3-7=-17$
distractors.B: took $-2$ times $-4$ as $-8$, missing that two negatives give a positive, and wrote $-4-8=-12$
distractors.D: grouped from the left as $(-4-2)(3-7)=(-6)(-4)=24$

questions.stem: The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=2-x^2$. What is the value of $g(-3)$?
questions.solution: Substitute with brackets: $g(-3)=2-(-3)^2$. The power acts on $-3$, giving $(-3)^2=9$, so $g(-3)=2-9=-7$.

distractors.B: replaced $(-3)^2$ with $-3\times 2=-6$, giving $2-(-6)=8$
distractors.D: subtracted before squaring, computing $(2-(-3))^2=5^2=25$

questions.stem: What is the value of $-7-(-3)-8+(-2)$?
What is the value of $-(4-9)-(-2-3)$?
questions.solution: Work inside the brackets first: $4-9=-5$ and $-2-3=-5$. The expression is $-(-5)-(-5)=5+5=10$.

distractors.A: distributed neither minus sign, computing $(-4-9)+(-2-3)$
distractors.B: applied the first minus to only the first term, computing $-4-9+5$
distractors.C: changed the sign of the first bracket but left the second as $-5$

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-1)^{15}+(-1)^{20}$?
questions.solution: An odd power of $-1$ is $-1$ and an even power of $-1$ is $1$, so the sum is $-1+1=0$.

distractors.A: treated both powers as $-1$, ignoring that $20$ is even
distractors.B: added the exponents first and evaluated $(-1)^{35}$
distractors.D: treated both powers as $1$, assuming a power is never negative

questions.stem: What is the value of $-2^4+(-2)^3$?
questions.solution: No bracket in the first term, so $-2^4=-(2^4)=-16$. The bracket in the second term gives $(-2)^3=-8$. Then $-16+(-8)=-24$.

questions.stem: If $x=-3$, what is the value of $-x^2$?
questions.solution: Substitute with a bracket: $-x^2=-(-3)^2=-(9)=-9$. The square acts on $-3$ first, then the leading minus is applied.

distractors.B: multiplied the base by the exponent, computing $-(-3)(2)$
distractors.C: multiplied the base by the exponent and dropped the sign
distractors.D: evaluated $(-3)^2=9$ and ignored the minus sign in front of $x^2$

questions.stem: If $x=-2$, what is the value of $x^3-x^2$?
Which expression is equivalent to $(x-8)(x-3)$?
questions.solution: The middle term is $-3x-8x=-11x$ and the constant is $(-8)(-3)=24$, giving $x^2-11x+24$.

distractors.B: kept the constant negative, forgetting that two negatives multiply to a positive
distractors.C: expanded $(x-8)(x+3)$ instead, using $-8+3$ for the middle term
distractors.D: added the sizes $8$ and $3$ for the middle term without carrying the negative signs

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(x+5)(x-9)$?
questions.solution: The middle term is $-9x+5x=-4x$ and the constant is $(5)(-9)=-45$, giving $x^2-4x-45$.

distractors.A: added the sizes $5$ and $9$ for the middle term instead of combining signed terms
distractors.B: made the constant positive, as if the two constants had matching signs
distractors.D: computed the middle coefficient as $9-5$ and attached the wrong sign

questions.stem: The expression $(x-6)^2$ can be written as $x^2+bx+c$, where $b$ and $c$ are constants. What is the value of $b$?
Which expression is equivalent to $(2x-3)(x-4)$?
questions.solution: The $x$ terms are $2x(-4)=-8x$ and $-3(x)=-3x$, which combine to $-11x$. The constant is $(-3)(-4)=12$.

distractors.A: combined $-8x$ and $-3x$ as $-8x+3x$, losing a sign
distractors.C: kept the constant negative instead of multiplying two negatives to a positive
distractors.B: took the middle coefficient as positive because both constants were negative

questions.stem: In the expansion of $(x-7)(x+2)$, what is the coefficient of $x$?
questions.solution: The two $x$ terms are $2x$ and $-7x$, and $2x-7x=-5x$. The coefficient is $-5$.

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=3x^2+2x$. What is the value of $f(-3)$?
The function $h$ is defined by $h(x)=-2x^2+5$. What is the value of $h(-4)$?

distractors.B: doubled the input instead of squaring it, computing $-2(2\cdot(-4))+5$
distractors.C: let the negative input cancel the coefficient's minus, computing $2(16)+5$
distractors.D: squared the whole product, computing $(-2\cdot(-4))^2+5$

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-1}{x+4}$. What is the value of $f(-7)$?
questions.solution: The numerator is $(-7)^2-1=49-1=48$ and the denominator is $-7+4=-3$. So $f(-7)=\dfrac{48}{-3}=-16$.

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2+4x-1$. What is the value of $f(-5)$?

distractors.A: wrote $(-5)^2$ as $-25$, computing $-25-20-1$
distractors.D: read $4(-5)$ as $+20$, computing $25+20-1$

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-3)^2-4(-2)(3)$?
What is the value of $\dfrac{-6+(-2)(-9)}{-4}$?
questions.solution: Multiply inside the numerator first: $(-2)(-9)=18$, so the numerator is $-6+18=12$. Then $\dfrac{12}{-4}=-3$.

distractors.A: added before multiplying, computing $\dfrac{(-6+(-2))(-9)}{-4}$
distractors.C: overlooked the negative sign on the denominator
distractors.D: took $(-2)(-9)$ as $-18$, giving a numerator of $-24$

questions.stem: Which of the following numbers is greatest?
questions.solution: As decimals the values are $-0.6$, $-0.5$, $-0.4$ and about $-0.333$. The greatest negative number is the one closest to zero, which is $-\dfrac{1}{3}$.

distractors.A: chose the value furthest from zero, treating the largest size as the largest value
distractors.B: picked the fraction with the smallest denominator while ignoring the negative sign
distractors.C: compared $-0.4$ with $-0.33$ and ranked them by digit size instead of position

questions.stem: On a number line, point $A$ is at $-11$ and point $B$ is at $4$. What is the distance between $A$ and $B$?
questions.solution: Distance is the size of the difference: $4-(-11)=4+11=15$ units.

questions.stem: What is the value of $|-7+2|$?
questions.solution: Evaluate inside the bars first: $-7+2=-5$. The absolute value gives the distance from zero, so $|-5|=5$.

distractors.A: added the two sizes inside the bars, computing $-(7+2)$
distractors.B: evaluated $-7+2=-5$ and left the negative sign in place
distractors.D: took the absolute value of $-7$ before adding, computing $7+2$

questions.stem: What is the value of $3^{-2}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $3^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{3^2}=\dfrac{1}{9}$.

distractors.A: assumed the negative exponent makes the value negative, computing $-(3^2)$
distractors.B: multiplied the base by the exponent, computing $3\cdot(-2)$
distractors.C: multiplied the base by the exponent inside the reciprocal, computing $\dfrac{1}{3\cdot 2}$

questions.stem: What is the value of $2^{-3}$?
What is the value of $(-2)^{-2}$?
questions.solution: First take the reciprocal: $(-2)^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{(-2)^2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$, since an even power of a negative number is positive.

distractors.A: read the exponent's minus as the sign of the answer and squared to get $4$
distractors.B: assumed the negative base keeps the result negative
distractors.D: ignored the negative exponent and evaluated $(-2)^2$

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $\dfrac{x}{-4}$?
questions.solution: A negative sign in the denominator can be written in front of the fraction instead: $\dfrac{x}{-4}=-\dfrac{x}{4}$.

distractors.B: dropped the negative sign when clearing it out of the denominator
distractors.C: swapped the numerator and the denominator, keeping the sign
distractors.D: swapped the numerator and the denominator and dropped the sign

questions.stem: What is the value of $-\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{1}{6}$?
questions.solution: Use a common denominator of $6$: $-\dfrac{4}{6}+\dfrac{1}{6}=-\dfrac{3}{6}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-2)^3(-3)^2-(-4)^2$?
questions.solution: Each power first: $(-2)^3=-8$ because an odd power of a negative stays negative; $(-3)^2=9$; $(-4)^2=16$. So the expression is $(-8)(9)-16=-72-16=-88$.

distractors.C: made $(-2)^3$ positive $8$, giving $72-16=56$
distractors.D: made $(-2)^3$ positive and also added the last term, giving $72+16=88$

questions.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=-x^2-4x$. What is the value of $f(-2)-f(-6)$?
What is the value of $\dfrac{(-2)^4(-3)^3}{(-6)^2}$?

distractors.B: multiplied each base by its exponent, computing $\dfrac{(-8)(-9)}{-12}$
distractors.C: multiplied each base by its exponent and then treated the quotient as positive
distractors.D: took $(-3)^3$ as $27$, since the base looked squared away to positive

questions.stem: The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=x^3+2x$. What is the value of $g(-2)+g(2)$?
Which expression is equivalent to $-2(x-4)-3(2x-5)$?

distractors.A: left both constants negative, using $-8$ and $-15$
distractors.B: handled the first bracket correctly but used $-3(-5)=-15$
distractors.C: wrote $-2(-4)$ as $-8$ while expanding the second bracket correctly

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(3-x)(x+5)$?
questions.solution: Expanding gives $3x+15-x^2-5x$. Combining the $x$ terms, $3x-5x=-2x$, so the result is $-x^2-2x+15$.

distractors.A: took the constant as $-15$, as if both constants were negative
distractors.C: combined $3x$ and $-5x$ as $+2x$, reversing the middle sign
distractors.D: expanded $(x-3)(x+5)$ instead, so every sign on the leading terms flipped

questions.stem: The expression $(2x-5)(3x-4)$ can be written as $ax^2+bx+c$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are constants. What is the value of $b$?
questions.solution: The $x$ terms are $2x(-4)=-8x$ and $-5(3x)=-15x$. Together, $-8x-15x=-23x$, so $b=-23$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-3-2\left[4-(-3)(2)\right]$?

distractors.A: combined $-3-2$ before using the bracket, computing $(-5)(10)$
distractors.C: took $-(-3)(2)$ as $-6$, giving a bracket value of $-2$
distractors.D: dropped the minus on the $2$, computing $-3+2(10)$

questions.stem: What is the value of $\dfrac{-2^3+(-4)^2}{-(-2)}$?
questions.solution: In the numerator, $-2^3=-(2^3)=-8$ and $(-4)^2=16$, so it equals $8$. The denominator is $-(-2)=2$. Then $\dfrac{8}{2}=4$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $2^{-3}(-2)^2$?
questions.solution: $2^{-3}=\dfrac{1}{8}$ and $(-2)^2=4$, so the product is $\dfrac{4}{8}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

distractors.A: read $2^{-3}$ as $-8$ and multiplied by $4$
distractors.B: took $(-2)^2$ as $-4$, keeping the sign through the squaring
distractors.D: read $2^{-3}$ as $8$, dropping the reciprocal, and multiplied by $4$

questions.stem: If $a<0$, which of the following expressions must be positive?
questions.solution: With $a$ negative, $a^3$ is negative because three negative factors give a negative product. So $-a^3$ is the opposite of a negative number, which is positive.

distractors.A: assumed an odd power of a negative number is positive
distractors.B: saw the square and stopped, overlooking the minus sign in front of $a^2$
distractors.C: assumed the square makes the whole product positive, ignoring the extra factor of $a$

questions.stem: What is the value of $(-2)(-3)(-4)(-5)(-6)$?
questions.solution: The sizes multiply to $2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6=720$. There are five negative factors, an odd count, so the product is negative: $-720$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-\dfrac{3}{4}-\left(-\dfrac{5}{6}\right)$?
questions.solution: Subtracting a negative adds it: $-\dfrac{3}{4}+\dfrac{5}{6}$. With denominator $12$ this is $-\dfrac{9}{12}+\dfrac{10}{12}=\dfrac{1}{12}$.

distractors.A: read $-\left(-\dfrac{5}{6}\right)$ as $-\dfrac{5}{6}$ and added two negatives
distractors.B: found the gap of $\dfrac{1}{12}$ but copied the sign of the first fraction
distractors.D: added the two sizes and reported the total as positive

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $-(3x-4)(x-2)$?
questions.solution: First expand: $(3x-4)(x-2)=3x^2-6x-4x+8=3x^2-10x+8$. The leading minus changes every sign, giving $-3x^2+10x-8$.

distractors.A: applied the leading minus to the first term only
distractors.C: flipped the first two terms but left the constant positive
distractors.D: expanded correctly and then did not apply the leading minus at all

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $5x-8=2x+7$?
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $3x-8=7$. Add $8$ to both sides: $3x=15$. Divide by $3$ to get $x=5$.

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $3(x+4)=x-2$?
questions.solution: Distribute on the left: $3x+12=x-2$. Subtract $x$: $2x+12=-2$. Subtract $12$: $2x=-14$, so $x=-7$. Checking, $3(-7+4)=-9$ and $-7-2=-9$.

distractors.B: distributed to the first term only, solving $3x+4=x-2$ to get $x=-3$
distractors.C: added $12$ to the right instead of subtracting it, solving $2x=-2+12=10$ to get $x=5$
distractors.D: made both of those sign slips, solving $2x=14$ to get $x=7$

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{x}{6}=5$?
questions.solution: Multiply every term by $6$, the least common denominator: $2x+x=30$. So $3x=30$ and $x=10$. Checking, $\dfrac{10}{3}+\dfrac{10}{6}=\dfrac{20}{6}+\dfrac{10}{6}=5$.

questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is given by $P=2L+2W$. Which equation gives $W$ in terms of $P$ and $L$?
questions.solution: Subtract $2L$ from both sides: $P-2L=2W$. Divide both sides by $2$: $W=\dfrac{P-2L}{2}$. Testing with $P=30$ and $L=7$ gives $W=8$, and $2(7)+2(8)=30$.

distractors.A: subtracted $2L$ but never divided by the coefficient $2$ on $W$
distractors.C: divided only the $P$ term by $2$, leaving $2L$ undivided
distractors.D: divided the whole right side by $2$ but dropped the coefficient on $L$ at the same time

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $0.4x+1.2=3.6$?
questions.solution: Multiply every term by $10$ to clear the decimals: $4x+12=36$. Subtract $12$: $4x=24$, so $x=6$. Checking, $0.4(6)+1.2=2.4+1.2=3.6$.

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $9-3x=24$?
questions.solution: Subtract $9$ from both sides: $-3x=15$. Divide both sides by $-3$: $x=-5$. Checking, $9-3(-5)=9+15=24$.

distractors.A: added $9$ to $24$ instead of subtracting it, then divided by $-3$ to get $-11$
distractors.C: divided $15$ by $3$ and kept the result positive, ignoring the negative coefficient
distractors.D: added $9$ to $24$ and also dropped the negative sign, giving $33\div 3=11$

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $7x-5=4x+16$?
questions.solution: Subtract $4x$ from both sides: $3x-5=16$. Add $5$ to both sides: $3x=21$, so $x=7$. Checking, $7(7)-5=44$ and $4(7)+16=44$.

questions.stem: What value of $x$ satisfies $8x+3=5x+18$?

questions.stem: The line through $(a,-1)$ and $(6,5)$ has slope $\dfrac{3}{4}$. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: Set up the slope: $\dfrac{5-(-1)}{6-a}=\dfrac{3}{4}$, so $\dfrac{6}{6-a}=\dfrac{3}{4}$. Cross-multiplying gives $24=3(6-a)$, so $8=6-a$ and $a=-2$. Checking, $\dfrac{5-(-1)}{6-(-2)}=\dfrac{6}{8}=\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.stem: A linear function $g$ satisfies $g(8)=-5$, $g(2)=13$, $g(6)=1$ and $g(4)=7$. What is the slope of the graph of $g$?
questions.solution: The inputs are out of order. Using $(2,13)$ and $(8,-5)$: $\dfrac{-5-13}{8-2}=\dfrac{-18}{6}=-3$. Using $(4,7)$ and $(6,1)$: $\dfrac{1-7}{6-4}=\dfrac{-6}{2}=-3$, which agrees.

questions.stem: Line $u$ has slope $-\dfrac{7}{2}$. Line $v$ has a positive slope and is exactly as steep as line $u$. What is the slope of line $v$?
questions.solution: Steepness is the distance of the slope from $0$, so $\left|-\dfrac{7}{2}\right|=\dfrac{7}{2}$. A line equally steep with a positive slope has slope $\dfrac{7}{2}=3.5$.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the graph of $8x-2y=6$ written in slope-intercept form?
questions.solution: Solve for $y$: $-2y=-8x+6$, so dividing by $-2$ gives $y=4x-3$. Checking the point $(1,1)$: $8(1)-2(1)=6$ and $4(1)-3=1$.

questions.stem: The line through $(-8,-1)$ and $(4,q)$ has slope $\dfrac{5}{6}$. What is the value of $q$?
questions.solution: Set up the slope: $\dfrac{q-(-1)}{4-(-8)}=\dfrac{5}{6}$, so $\dfrac{q+1}{12}=\dfrac{5}{6}$. Then $6(q+1)=60$, so $q+1=10$ and $q=9$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $6x+ky=9$ is parallel to the graph of $y=\dfrac{2}{3}x-4$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: Solving $6x+ky=9$ for $y$ gives $y=-\dfrac{6}{k}x+\dfrac{9}{k}$. Parallel lines have equal slopes, so $-\dfrac{6}{k}=\dfrac{2}{3}$. Then $-18=2k$ and $k=-9$. Checking, $-\dfrac{6}{-9}=\dfrac{2}{3}$.

distractors.C: solved $\dfrac{6}{k}=\dfrac{3}{2}$ after inverting the slope and dropping the sign

questions.stem: The line through $(-4,9)$ and $(6,k)$ is perpendicular to a line of slope $\dfrac{5}{2}$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: A line perpendicular to one of slope $\dfrac{5}{2}$ has slope $-\dfrac{2}{5}$. So $\dfrac{k-9}{6-(-4)}=-\dfrac{2}{5}$, which is $\dfrac{k-9}{10}=-\dfrac{2}{5}$. Then $k-9=10\cdot\left(-\dfrac{2}{5}\right)=-4$, so $k=5$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $ax+3y=12$ is parallel to the graph of $y=-4x+1$. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: Write $ax+3y=12$ in slope-intercept form: $3y=-ax+12$, so $y=-\dfrac{a}{3}x+4$ and the slope is $-\dfrac{a}{3}$. Parallel lines have equal slopes, so $-\dfrac{a}{3}=-4$. Multiplying both sides by $-3$ gives $a=12$. Then $12x+3y=12$ becomes $y=-4x+4$, which is parallel to the given line.

distractors.B: read the coefficient of $x$ in standard form as the slope, so set $a=-4$

questions.stem: The line through $(-6,t)$ and $(2,5)$ is parallel to the graph of $3x+4y=8$. What is the value of $t$?
questions.solution: Rewrite $3x+4y=8$ as $4y=-3x+8$, so $y=-\dfrac{3}{4}x+2$ and the slope is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. A parallel line has the same slope, so $\dfrac{5-t}{2-(-6)}=-\dfrac{3}{4}$, that is $\dfrac{5-t}{8}=-\dfrac{3}{4}$. Then $5-t=-6$, so $t=11$.

questions.stem: The points $(-3,11)$ and $(5,-5)$ lie on line $\ell$ in the $xy$-plane. Line $\ell$ crosses the $y$-axis at the point $(0,b)$. What is the value of $b$?
questions.solution: The slope is $\dfrac{-5-11}{5-(-3)}=\dfrac{-16}{8}=-2$. Starting at $(-3,11)$ and moving $3$ units right lowers $y$ by $2(3)=6$, so $b=11-6=5$. Checking with the other point, $-2(5)+5=-5$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, line $\ell$ has $x$-intercept $(-6,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,4)$. Which equation represents a line perpendicular to line $\ell$?
questions.solution: Line $\ell$ has slope $\dfrac{4-0}{0-(-6)}=\dfrac{4}{6}=\dfrac{2}{3}$. The negative reciprocal is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$, so any line with slope $-\dfrac{3}{2}$ is perpendicular to $\ell$. The $y$-intercept of the perpendicular line can be anything.

questions.stem: A linear function $f$ satisfies $f(-4)=13$ and $f(6)=-7$. What is the value of $f(1)$?
questions.solution: The slope is $\dfrac{-7-13}{6-(-4)}=\dfrac{-20}{10}=-2$. From $x=-4$ to $x=1$ the input increases by $5$, so the output changes by $-2(5)=-10$. Therefore $f(1)=13-10=3$.

questions.stem: The points $(-2,7)$, $(0,c)$ and $(4,-5)$ all lie on the same line in the $xy$-plane. What is the value of $c$?
questions.solution: Using the outer points, the slope is $\dfrac{-5-7}{4-(-2)}=\dfrac{-12}{6}=-2$. From $x=-2$ to $x=0$ the input increases by $2$, so the output changes by $-2(2)=-4$. Therefore $c=7-4=3$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, line $m$ passes through the origin and is parallel to the line through $(-3,-4)$ and $(5,2)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on line $m$ whose $x$-coordinate is $12$?
questions.solution: The slope of the given line is $\dfrac{2-(-4)}{5-(-3)}=\dfrac{6}{8}=\dfrac{3}{4}$. Parallel lines share that slope, and line $m$ passes through $(0,0)$, so $y=\dfrac{3}{4}x$. At $x=12$, $y=\dfrac{3}{4}(12)=9$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, line $\ell$ is the graph of $5x-2y=8$. Line $n$ is perpendicular to line $\ell$ and passes through $(10,-1)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of line $n$?
questions.solution: Solving $5x-2y=8$ for $y$ gives $y=\dfrac{5}{2}x-4$, so line $\ell$ has slope $\dfrac{5}{2}$ and line $n$ has slope $-\dfrac{2}{5}$. Substituting $(10,-1)$: $-1=-\dfrac{2}{5}(10)+b=-4+b$, so $b=3$.

questions.stem: Which of the following lines in the $xy$-plane is the steepest?
questions.solution: The four slopes are $2$, $-\dfrac{3}{2}$, $-\dfrac{9}{4}$ and $\dfrac{11}{5}$. Steepness is the distance from $0$: $2$, $1.5$, $2.25$ and $2.2$. The largest is $2.25$, so the graph of $y=-\dfrac{9}{4}x+1$ is the steepest.

questions.stem: The amount of water in a tank decreases at a constant rate. The tank holds $92$ liters after $2$ hours and $68$ liters after $8$ hours. How many liters of water were in the tank at the start?
questions.solution: The rate of change is $\dfrac{68-92}{8-2}=\dfrac{-24}{6}=-4$ liters per hour. Going back $2$ hours from the $2$-hour reading adds $4(2)=8$ liters, so the starting amount is $92+8=100$ liters.

questions.solution: The given line has slope $\dfrac{-2-4}{5-1}=\dfrac{-6}{4}=-\dfrac{3}{2}$. Rewriting $6x-ay=11$ gives $y=\dfrac{6}{a}x-\dfrac{11}{a}$, so $\dfrac{6}{a}=-\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $a=-4$. Checking: $6x+4y=11$ has slope $-\dfrac{3}{2}$.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $ax+3y=12$ has $x$-intercept $-4$, where $a$ is a constant. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: An $x$-intercept of $-4$ means the point $(-4,0)$ is on the graph. Substituting: $a(-4)+3(0)=12$, so $-4a=12$ and $a=-3$. Checking: $-3(-4)+0=12$.

questions.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane crosses the $y$-axis at $(0,-3)$ and passes through the point $(6,1)$. At what value of $x$ does this line cross the $x$-axis?
questions.solution: The slope is $\dfrac{1-(-3)}{6-0}=\dfrac{4}{6}=\dfrac{2}{3}$, so the line is $y=\dfrac{2}{3}x-3$. Setting $y=0$ gives $\dfrac{2}{3}x=3$, so $x=4.5$. Checking: $\dfrac{2}{3}(4.5)-3=0$.

questions.stem: In the system $y=2x-1$ and $3x+y=14$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: The first equation already gives $y$ on its own, so substitution costs the least work. Replace $y$ in the second equation: $3x+(2x-1)=14$. Then $5x-1=14$, so $5x=15$ and $x=3$. Check: $y=2(3)-1=5$, and $3(3)+5=14$.

questions.stem: Three pens and two notebooks cost 12 dollars. One pen and two notebooks cost 8 dollars. All pens cost the same, and all notebooks cost the same. What is the cost, in dollars, of one pen?
questions.solution: Let $p$ be the price of a pen and $n$ the price of a notebook. Then $3p+2n=12$ and $p+2n=8$. The $n$-coefficients match, so subtracting gives $2p=4$ and $p=2$. Then $2n=8-2=6$, so $n=3$. Check: $3(2)+2(3)=12$.

questions.solution: Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width. Perimeter gives $2(L+W)=46$, so $L+W=23$, and the relation gives $L-W=5$. Adding these two equations gives $2L=28$, so $L=14$ and $W=9$. Check: $2(14+9)=46$.

questions.stem: The system $0.3x+0.4y=3.3$ and $0.5x-0.2y=2.9$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Multiply both equations by $10$: $3x+4y=33$ and $5x-2y=29$. Doubling the second gives $10x-4y=58$, and adding that to $3x+4y=33$ gives $13x=91$, so $x=7$. Then $3(7)+4y=33$ gives $y=3$. Check: $0.5(7)-0.2(3)=3.5-0.6=2.9$.

questions.stem: The system $\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{y}{4}=5$ and $x-y=1$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $y$?
questions.solution: Multiply the first equation by $12$: $4x+3y=60$. From $x-y=1$, $x=y+1$, so $4(y+1)+3y=60$, giving $7y=56$ and $y=8$. Then $x=9$. Check: $\dfrac{9}{3}+\dfrac{8}{4}=3+2=5$.

questions.stem: The system $4x+6y=11$ and $2x+ky=5$ has no solution. What is the value of the constant $k$?
questions.solution: No solution means the lines are parallel and distinct, so the $x$- and $y$-coefficients must be in the same ratio. Here $\dfrac{4}{2}=2$, so $\dfrac{6}{k}=2$ and $k=3$. With $k=3$ the system is $4x+6y=11$ and $2x+3y=5$; doubling the second gives $4x+6y=10$, which contradicts $4x+6y=11$, so the lines really are parallel and distinct.

distractors.C: built the ratio from the constants, using $\dfrac{11}{2}$
distractors.D: doubled the $6$ instead of halving it, scaling in the wrong direction

questions.stem: The system $2x+3y=7$ and $10x+15y=k$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of the constant $k$?
questions.solution: Infinitely many solutions means the two equations describe the same line. The second equation's coefficients are $5$ times the first's, since $10=5(2)$ and $15=5(3)$, so the constant must be scaled the same way: $k=5(7)=35$. Then $10x+15y=35$ is exactly $5$ times $2x+3y=7$, the same line twice.

questions.stem: The system $5x-2y=9$ and $ax-6y=20$ has no solution. What is the value of the constant $a$?
questions.solution: Parallel distinct lines need matching coefficient ratios. The $y$-coefficient goes from $-2$ to $-6$, a factor of $3$, so $a=3(5)=15$. With $a=15$ the second equation is $15x-6y=20$, while tripling the first gives $15x-6y=27$. The two constants differ, so the lines are parallel and distinct and there is no solution.

distractors.B: found the multiplier $3$ and reported it in place of $a$
distractors.C: left $a$ equal to the $x$-coefficient of the first equation

questions.stem: A technician mixes a 20 percent salt solution with a 50 percent salt solution to make 30 litres of a 30 percent salt solution. How many litres of the 50 percent solution are used?
questions.solution: Let $a$ and $b$ be the litres of the 20 percent and 50 percent solutions. Volume gives $a+b=30$, and salt gives $0.2a+0.5b=0.3(30)=9$. Substituting $a=30-b$: $0.2(30-b)+0.5b=9$, so $6+0.3b=9$, giving $0.3b=3$ and $b=10$. Then $a=20$. Check: $0.2(20)+0.5(10)=4+5=9$.

questions.stem: A concert sold 180 tickets and collected 2,140 dollars. Floor tickets cost 15 dollars each and balcony tickets cost 8 dollars each. How many floor tickets were sold?
questions.solution: Let $a$ be floor tickets and $b$ balcony tickets. Then $a+b=180$ and $15a+8b=2140$. Substituting $b=180-a$ gives $15a+8(180-a)=2140$, so $7a+1440=2140$ and $7a=700$, giving $a=100$ and $b=80$. Check: $15(100)+8(80)=1500+640=2140$.

distractors.C: rounded the balcony price to 5 dollars and solved $15a+5b=2140$ with $a+b=180$
distractors.D: stopped at $7a=700$ without dividing by $7$

questions.stem: A rental company charges a one-time fee plus a fixed amount per day. Three days cost 155 dollars and seven days cost 315 dollars. What would five days cost, in dollars?
questions.solution: Let $r$ be the daily rate and $f$ the fee. Then $3r+f=155$ and $7r+f=315$. The $f$-coefficients match, so subtracting gives $4r=160$ and $r=40$; then $f=155-3(40)=35$. Five days cost $5(40)+35=235$ dollars. Check: $7(40)+35=315$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perimeter 64 metres, and its length is 3 times its width. What is the length, in metres?
questions.solution: Let $L$ and $W$ be length and width. Perimeter gives $2(L+W)=64$, so $L+W=32$, and the relation gives $L=3W$. Substituting, $3W+W=32$, so $4W=32$ and $W=8$, making $L=24$. Check: $2(24+8)=64$.

distractors.D: used $L+W=64$ instead of $L+W=32$, forgetting the factor of $2$ in the perimeter

questions.stem: The system $5x+2y=44$ and $x=4y$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: It is quicker to find $y$ first. Substituting $x=4y$ gives $5(4y)+2y=44$, so $22y=44$ and $y=2$. Then $x=4(2)=8$. Check: $5(8)+2(2)=40+4=44$.

questions.stem: The system $0.6x+0.8y=4.8$ and $1.5x-0.4y=4.8$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Double the second equation: $3x-0.8y=9.6$. Adding it to $0.6x+0.8y=4.8$ removes $y$: $3.6x=14.4$, so $x=4$. Then $0.6(4)+0.8y=4.8$ gives $0.8y=2.4$ and $y=3$. Check: $1.5(4)-0.4(3)=6-1.2=4.8$.

distractors.D: divided $4.8$ by $0.6$ in the first equation while ignoring the $0.8y$ term

questions.stem: The system $6x+5y=58$ and $6x-5y=2$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: The $y$-coefficients are opposites, so adding the equations gives $12x=60$ and $x=5$. (Then $5y=58-30=28$, so $y=5.6$.) Check: $6(5)-5(5.6)=30-28=2$.

questions.stem: The system $6x+ay=12$ and $9x+6y=b$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $a+b$?
questions.solution: Infinitely many solutions means the same line twice. The $x$-coefficient goes from $6$ to $9$, a factor of $\dfrac{3}{2}$, so every part scales the same way: $6=\dfrac{3}{2}a$ gives $a=4$, and $b=\dfrac{3}{2}(12)=18$. Then $6x+4y=12$ and $9x+6y=18$ are the same line, and $a+b=22$.

If $7x+2y=46$ and $5x+10y=50$, what is the value of $x+y$?

Because those two sums match, adding the equations as they stand gives a multiple of $x+y$: $12x+12y=46+50=96$, so $12(x+y)=96$ and $x+y=8$. (Solving fully gives $x=6$ and $y=2$, which agrees.)

questions.stem: The system $5x+2y=7$ and $ax+6y=11$ has no solution. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: Parallel distinct lines have proportional coefficients but constants that do not match the same ratio. The $y$-coefficients give the scale factor $6/2=3$, so $a=3(5)=15$. Then the second equation reads $15x+6y=11$, while tripling the first gives $15x+6y=21$. Since $11\\ne 21$ the lines are parallel and distinct, so there is no solution.

questions.stem: The system $cx+4y=10$ and $6x+8y=d$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $c+d$?
questions.solution: Infinitely many solutions means the equations describe the same line. The $y$-coefficients give the scale factor $8/4=2$, so the second equation is twice the first. That forces $6=2c$, giving $c=3$, and $d=2(10)=20$. Therefore $c+d=3+20=23$. Check: $2(3x+4y=10)$ gives $6x+8y=20$.

questions.stem: A copy shop charges a one-time setup fee plus a fixed amount per page. An order of 8 pages costs 14 dollars and an order of 20 pages costs 26 dollars. What would an order of 35 pages cost, in dollars?
questions.solution: Let $f$ be the setup fee and $p$ the charge per page. Then $f+8p=14$ and $f+20p=26$. The $f$-coefficients match, so subtracting gives $12p=12$ and $p=1$. Then $f=14-8(1)=6$. An order of 35 pages costs $6+35(1)=41$ dollars. Check: $6+20(1)=26$.

questions.stem: One data plan costs 20 dollars a month plus 0.10 dollars per minute of calls. Another costs 35 dollars a month plus 0.05 dollars per minute. For how many minutes of calls do the two plans cost the same amount?
questions.solution: Let $c$ be the monthly cost and $m$ the minutes. The system is $c=20+0.10m$ and $c=35+0.05m$. Since $c$ is isolated in both, set them equal: $20+0.10m=35+0.05m$, so $0.05m=15$ and $m=300$. Check: $20+0.10(300)=50$ and $35+0.05(300)=50$.

questions.stem: If $7x+5y=62$ and $9x+3y=66$, what is the value of $x-y$?
questions.solution: The coefficients in each equation total $12$, so subtracting the first equation from the second keeps the $x$- and $y$-terms equal and opposite: $(9x+3y)-(7x+5y)=2x-2y=66-62=4$. Dividing by $2$ gives $x-y=2$. (Solving fully gives $x=6$ and $y=4$, and $6-4=2$.)

questions.stem: If $0.6x+0.2y=3.6$ and $0.2x+0.6y=2.8$, what is the value of $x+y$?
questions.solution: The coefficients $0.6$ and $0.2$ appear in both equations with $x$ and $y$ swapped, so the sum is symmetric: $(0.6x+0.2y)+(0.2x+0.6y)=0.8x+0.8y=3.6+2.8=6.4$. Dividing by $0.8$ gives $x+y=8$. (Solving fully gives $x=5$ and $y=3$, and $5+3=8$.)

questions.stem: If $7x+2y=48$ and $4x+6y=42$, what is the value of $x-y$?
questions.solution: Subtracting gives $3x-4y=6$, where $3$ and $-4$ are not equal and opposite, so this is not a multiple of $x-y$ and no shortcut applies. Solve instead: multiply the first equation by $3$ to get $21x+6y=144$ and subtract $4x+6y=42$, giving $17x=102$ and $x=6$. Then $7(6)+2y=48$ gives $y=3$, so $x-y=3$. Check: $4(6)+6(3)=42$.

questions.stem: The system $2x+(k-1)y=8$ and $6x+9y=5$ has no solution. What is the value of the constant $k$?
questions.solution: Parallel distinct lines need matching coefficient ratios. The $x$-coefficient goes from $2$ to $6$, a factor of $3$, so $9=3(k-1)$, giving $k-1=3$ and $k=4$. With $k=4$ the first equation is $2x+3y=8$; tripling it gives $6x+9y=24$, which contradicts $6x+9y=5$, so the lines are parallel and distinct and there is no solution.

questions.stem: The system $4x-6y=c$ and $dx-9y=12$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $c+d$?
questions.solution: The same line twice means every coefficient scales by one factor. The $y$-coefficient goes from $-6$ to $-9$, a factor of $\dfrac{3}{2}$, so $d=\dfrac{3}{2}(4)=6$ and $12=\dfrac{3}{2}c$, giving $c=8$. Then $4x-6y=8$ and $6x-9y=12$ are the same line, and $c+d=14$.

questions.stem: A shop mixes almonds costing 9 dollars per pound with raisins costing 4 dollars per pound to make 20 pounds of a mix worth 6 dollars per pound. How many pounds of almonds are used?
questions.solution: Let $a$ and $r$ be pounds of almonds and raisins. Then $a+r=20$ and $9a+4r=6(20)=120$. Substituting $r=20-a$ gives $9a+4(20-a)=120$, so $5a+80=120$ and $a=8$, making $r=12$. Check: $9(8)+4(12)=72+48=120$.

distractors.B: split the 20 pounds evenly because 6 lies between 4 and 9
distractors.C: gave the pounds of raisins instead
distractors.D: divided the total value $120$ by the almond price $9$

questions.stem: A boat travels 36 kilometres downstream in 2 hours and the same 36 kilometres upstream in 3 hours. What is the boat's speed in still water, in kilometres per hour?
questions.solution: Let $b$ be the boat's speed in still water and $c$ the current's speed. Downstream the speed is $b+c=\dfrac{36}{2}=18$, and upstream it is $b-c=\dfrac{36}{3}=12$. Adding gives $2b=30$, so $b=15$, and then $c=3$. Check: $36\div(15+3)=2$ hours and $36\div(15-3)=3$ hours.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the line $y=ax+3$ passes through the solution of the system $2x+y=11$ and $3x+y=13$. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: The $y$-coefficients match, so subtracting gives $x=2$, and then $2(2)+y=11$ gives $y=7$. The point $(2,7)$ lies on $y=ax+3$, so $7=2a+3$, giving $2a=4$ and $a=2$. Check: $3(2)+7=13$.

questions.stem: The system $5x+7y=70$ and $3x-4y=1$ has solution $(x,y)$. What is the value of $y$?
questions.solution: Neither pair of coefficients matches, so scale both equations. Multiply the first by $3$ and the second by $5$: $15x+21y=210$ and $15x-20y=5$. Subtracting gives $41y=205$, so $y=5$. Then $5x+7(5)=70$ gives $5x=35$ and $x=7$. Check: $3(7)-4(5)=21-20=1$.

questions.stem: A school paid 4,300 dollars for 12 tablets and 5 printers, and 2,820 dollars for 8 tablets and 3 printers. All tablets cost the same and all printers cost the same. What is the price, in dollars, of one printer?
questions.solution: Let $t$ and $p$ be the prices. Then $12t+5p=4300$ and $8t+3p=2820$. Multiply the first by $2$ and the second by $3$: $24t+10p=8600$ and $24t+9p=8460$. Subtracting gives $p=140$. Then $8t+3(140)=2820$ gives $8t=2400$ and $t=300$. Check: $12(300)+5(140)=3600+700=4300$.

questions.stem: The system $(k+1)x+6y=15$ and $4x+8y=20$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of the constant $k$?
questions.solution: The same line twice means one factor scales everything. The $y$-coefficient goes from $6$ to $8$, a factor of $\dfrac{4}{3}$, and the constant matches that, since $\dfrac{4}{3}(15)=20$. So $4=\dfrac{4}{3}(k+1)$, giving $k+1=3$ and $k=2$. With $k=2$ the equations are $3x+6y=15$ and $4x+8y=20$, both of which reduce to $x+2y=5$.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $-3x>12$?
questions.solution: Divide both sides by $-3$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality, so $x<-4$. Test $x=-5$: $-3(-5)=15>12$, true. Test $x=-3$: $-3(-3)=9>12$, false. The solution is $x<-4$.

questions.stem: What is the greatest value of $x$ that satisfies $5x-7\le 18$?
questions.solution: Add 7 to both sides: $5x\le 25$. Divide by 5, a positive number, so the direction is unchanged: $x\le 5$. The greatest allowed value is 5. Test $x=5$: $5(5)-7=18\le 18$, true. Test $x=5.1$: $5(5.1)-7=18.5\le 18$, false.

questions.stem: Toni has saved 40 dollars and adds 11 dollars each week. She wants her savings to be at least 150 dollars. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of weeks $w$?
questions.solution: After $w$ weeks her savings are $40+11w$ dollars. The phrase at least 150 means the total may equal 150 or be larger, which is $\ge 150$. So the inequality is $40+11w\ge 150$.

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $20-4x>0$?
questions.solution: Subtract 20 from both sides: $-4x>-20$. Divide by $-4$ and reverse the direction: $x<5$. The inequality is strict, so 5 itself is excluded and the greatest integer allowed is 4. Test $x=4$: $20-16=4>0$, true. Test $x=5$: $20-20=0>0$, false.

questions.stem: A freight lift can carry no more than 1,200 pounds. The operator weighs 210 pounds and each box weighs 45 pounds. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of boxes $b$ the lift can carry with the operator aboard?
questions.solution: The operator and the boxes together must come to at most 1,200 pounds, so $210+45b\le 1200$. That gives $45b\le 990$, so $b\le 22$. A load of exactly 22 boxes weighs $210+990=1200$ pounds, which is allowed, so the inequality has to be inclusive.

questions.stem: A greenhouse control keeps the temperature $t$, in degrees, between 68 and 72, and neither 68 nor 72 is an allowed temperature. Which inequality describes the allowed values of $t$?
questions.solution: Between 68 and 72 places $t$ above 68 and below 72. Because neither endpoint is allowed, both comparisons are strict, giving $68<t<72$. A value such as 70 is allowed, while 68 and 72 are not.

questions.stem: A parking garage holds no more than 320 cars, and 185 cars are already parked there. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of additional cars $c$ the garage can take?
questions.solution: The total number of cars is $185+c$. The phrase "no more than 320" means the total can equal $320$ but cannot exceed it, so the total is at most $320$: $185+c\le 320$.

questions.stem: A van can carry a load of no more than 900 pounds. The driver weighs 160 pounds and each crate weighs 55 pounds. What is the greatest number of crates the van can carry with the driver aboard?
questions.solution: If $c$ is the number of crates, the load is $160+55c$, and this must be at most $900$: $160+55c\le 900$. Subtract $160$: $55c\le 740$. Divide by $55$: $c\le 13.4545\ldots$. Since $c$ counts whole crates, the greatest number is $13$, giving $160+715=875$ pounds. Fourteen crates would give $930$ pounds.

questions.stem: Maya has 96 points in a reading program and earns 12 points for each book she finishes. She wants to have at least 240 points. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of books $b$?
questions.solution: Her total is $96+12b$. The phrase "at least 240" means the total can equal $240$ or be larger, so the correct symbol is $\ge$: $96+12b\ge 240$.

distractors.B: read "at least" as the strict $>$, which would rule out a total of exactly 240
distractors.C: pointed the inequality the wrong way, describing a total of at most 240
distractors.D: ignored the 96 points she already has

questions.stem: What is the least value of $x$ that satisfies $4x-9\ge 3$?
questions.solution: Add $9$ to both sides: $4x\ge 12$. Divide by $4$, a positive number, so the direction stays: $x\ge 3$. The boundary value $3$ is included because $4(3)-9=3\ge 3$. Any smaller value, such as $2$, gives $-1\ge 3$, which is false.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $-\dfrac{x}{4}<3$?
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by $-4$. Multiplying by a negative number reverses the inequality, so $x>3(-4)$, that is $x>-12$. Testing $x=0$ gives $0<3$, true; testing $x=-16$ gives $4<3$, false.

distractors.B: dropped the negative sign in front of the fraction and multiplied by $4$
distractors.D: divided $3$ by $4$ instead of multiplying by $4$

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $8-2x>1$?
questions.solution: Subtract $8$ from both sides: $-2x>-7$. Divide by $-2$ and reverse the inequality: $x<\dfrac{7}{2}$, or $x<3.5$. The greatest integer below $3.5$ is $3$. Checking, $x=3$ gives $8-6=2>1$, true, while $x=4$ gives $8-8=0>1$, false.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the line $y=x+2$ is graphed as a dashed line, and the region above the line is shaded. Which inequality describes the shaded region?
questions.solution: Points above the line have $y$-values larger than the line's $y$-value at the same $x$, so the region is $y>x+2$. The line is dashed, which means points on the line are not part of the region, so the inequality is strict rather than inclusive.

distractors.B: described the region below the line instead of above it
distractors.C: described the region below the line and also included the dashed boundary

questions.stem: Which of the following points lies in the solution region of $y\le 2x-1$?
questions.solution: Substitute each point. For $(3,1)$: $2(3)-1=5$ and $1\le 5$ is true. For $(0,0)$: $2(0)-1=-1$ and $0\le -1$ is false. For $(1,4)$: $4\le 1$ is false. For $(2,5)$: $5\le 3$ is false.

distractors.C: swapped the $x$- and $y$-coordinates before substituting

questions.stem: What is the least value of $x$ that satisfies $-6x\le -30$?
questions.solution: Divide both sides by $-6$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality, so $x\ge \dfrac{-30}{-6}=5$. The boundary value $5$ is allowed because $-6(5)=-30\le -30$. Any smaller value, such as $4$, gives $-24\le -30$, which is false.

questions.stem: A team wants to spend fewer than 500 dollars in total on shirts that cost 18 dollars each. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of shirts $s$?
questions.solution: The cost of $s$ shirts is $18s$ dollars. The phrase "fewer than 500 dollars" means the cost must stay below $500$ and cannot equal it, so the strict symbol is needed: $18s<500$.

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $3(x+2)<20$?
questions.solution: Distribute: $3x+6<20$. Subtract $6$: $3x<14$. Divide by $3$: $x<\dfrac{14}{3}$, which is about $4.67$. The greatest integer below that is $4$. Checking, $x=4$ gives $3(6)=18<20$, true, while $x=5$ gives $3(7)=21<20$, false.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $10-x\ge 4$?
questions.solution: Subtract $10$ from both sides: $-x\ge -6$. Multiply both sides by $-1$ and reverse the inequality: $x\le 6$. Testing $x=6$ gives $4\ge 4$, true, and $x=7$ gives $3\ge 4$, false.

questions.stem: A club has 200 dollars to spend on a party. One banner costs 35 dollars and each pack of balloons costs 12 dollars. What is the greatest number of balloon packs the club can buy along with the banner?
questions.solution: If $p$ is the number of packs, the cost is $35+12p$ dollars, and this must be at most $200$: $35+12p\le 200$. Subtract $35$: $12p\le 165$. Divide by $12$: $p\le 13.75$. Since $p$ counts whole packs, the greatest number is $13$, costing $35+156=191$ dollars. Fourteen packs would cost $203$ dollars.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $4-7x<25$?
questions.solution: Subtract 4 from both sides: $-7x<21$. Divide by $-7$ and reverse the direction: $x>-3$. Test $x=-2$: $4-7(-2)=18<25$, true. Test $x=-4$: $4-7(-4)=32<25$, false. The solution is $x>-3$.

questions.solution: Subtract 1 from both sides: $-\frac{2}{3}x\ge 4$. Multiply both sides by $-\frac{3}{2}$, a negative number, so the direction reverses: $x\le -6$. Test $x=-6$: $-\frac{2}{3}(-6)+1=5\ge 5$, true. Test $x=-5$: $\frac{10}{3}+1\approx 4.33\ge 5$, false.

questions.stem: What is the least value of $x$ that satisfies $9-2x\le 4x-15$?
questions.solution: Add $2x$ to both sides and add 15 to both sides: $24\le 6x$. Divide by 6, a positive number, so the direction is unchanged: $4\le x$, that is $x\ge 4$. The least allowed value is 4. Test $x=4$: $9-8=1$ and $16-15=1$, and $1\le 1$, true. Test $x=3.9$: $1.2\le 0.6$, false.

questions.stem: Ravi has 60 dollars and buys notebooks costing 7 dollars each. He wants more than 20 dollars left over. What is the greatest number of notebooks he can buy?
questions.solution: With $n$ notebooks he has $60-7n$ dollars left, and more than 20 means $60-7n>20$. Subtract 60: $-7n>-40$. Divide by $-7$ and reverse the direction: $n<\frac{40}{7}$, about 5.71. Since $n$ counts notebooks, the greatest value is 5. Check: 5 notebooks leave 25 dollars, which is more than 20; 6 notebooks leave 18 dollars, which is not.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $-7\le 3-2x<5$?
questions.solution: Subtract 3 from all three parts: $-10\le -2x<2$. Divide all three parts by $-2$, reversing both inequality signs and swapping the ends: $5\ge x>-1$, which is $-1<x\le 5$. Test $x=5$: $3-10=-7$, and $-7\le -7<5$, true. Test $x=-1$: $3+2=5$, and $5<5$ is false, so $-1$ is excluded.

questions.solution: Test the origin $(0,0)$ in the boundary expression: $2(0)-3=-3$, and $0>-3$, so the origin satisfies $y>2x-3$. That is the shaded side. A dashed boundary means points on the line are excluded, so the sign stays strict and the answer is $y>2x-3$. Checking a point on the other side, $(0,-5)$ gives $-5>-3$, which is false.

questions.stem: A shop orders books in boxes of 25. The manager wants the order to contain fewer than 500 books. What is the greatest number of boxes the manager can order?
questions.solution: With $b$ boxes the order holds $25b$ books, and fewer than 500 means $25b<500$. Dividing by 25, a positive number, gives $b<20$. Because the inequality is strict, 20 boxes are not allowed. The greatest number is 19. Check: $25(19)=475$, which is fewer than 500; $25(20)=500$, which is not fewer than 500.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $5x+4>9x-8$?
questions.solution: Subtract $9x$ from both sides: $-4x+4>-8$. Subtract $4$: $-4x>-12$. Divide by $-4$ and reverse the inequality: $x<3$. Testing $x=2$ gives $14>10$, true; testing $x=4$ gives $24>28$, false.

questions.stem: What is the greatest value of $x$ that satisfies $2x+1\ge 6x-11$?
questions.solution: Subtract $6x$ from both sides: $-4x+1\ge -11$. Subtract $1$: $-4x\ge -12$. Divide by $-4$ and reverse the inequality: $x\le 3$. The boundary $3$ is allowed because $2(3)+1=7$ and $6(3)-11=7$, so $7\ge 7$. For $x=4$, $9\ge 13$ is false.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $4(x-1)\le 2(x+5)$?
questions.solution: Distribute on both sides: $4x-4\le 2x+10$. Subtract $2x$: $2x-4\le 10$. Add $4$: $2x\le 14$. Divide by $2$: $x\le 7$. Testing $x=7$ gives $24\le 24$, true, and $x=8$ gives $28\le 26$, false.

questions.solution: The pressure can be as low as $30$ and as high as $45$, and both of those values are acceptable, so both ends are inclusive. Written as a compound inequality this is $30\le p\le 45$.

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $4-3x>-11$?
questions.solution: Subtract $4$ from both sides: $-3x>-15$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse the inequality: $x<5$. Because $5$ itself is not allowed, the greatest integer is $4$. Checking, $x=4$ gives $4-12=-8>-11$, true, while $x=5$ gives $4-15=-11>-11$, false.

questions.stem: What is the least value of $x$ that satisfies $5-4x\le 2-x$?
questions.solution: Add $x$ to both sides: $5-3x\le 2$. Subtract $5$: $-3x\le -3$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse the inequality: $x\ge 1$. The boundary $1$ works because $5-4=1$ and $2-1=1$, so $1\le 1$. For $x=0$, $5\le 2$ is false.

questions.solution: The total charge is the one-time fee plus the monthly charge: $45+28m$ dollars. "No more than 325 dollars" means the total is at most $325$, so $45+28m\le 325$.

questions.stem: A caterer has 500 dollars for an event. There is a setup charge of 86 dollars and each meal costs 14 dollars. What is the greatest number of meals the caterer can order?
questions.solution: If $n$ is the number of meals, the cost is $86+14n$ dollars and this must be at most $500$: $86+14n\le 500$. Subtract $86$: $14n\le 414$. Divide by $14$: $n\le 29.57\ldots$. Since $n$ counts whole meals, the greatest number is $29$, costing $86+406=492$ dollars. Thirty meals would cost $506$ dollars.

questions.stem: A shaded region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the straight line through $(0,6)$ and $(3,0)$, and every point of the region lies on or below that line. Which inequality describes the region?
questions.solution: The boundary has slope $\dfrac{0-6}{3-0}=-2$ and $y$-intercept $6$, so its equation is $y=-2x+6$. Points below it have smaller $y$-values at the same $x$, and "on or below" includes the line itself, so the region is $y\le -2x+6$.

questions.stem: An elevator can hold a load of at most 2,000 pounds. Three workers inside weigh 540 pounds in total, and each toolbox weighs 65 pounds. What is the greatest number of toolboxes they can bring?
questions.solution: If $t$ is the number of toolboxes, the load is $540+65t$ and this must be at most $2{,}000$: $540+65t\le 2000$. Subtract $540$: $65t\le 1460$. Divide by $65$: $t\le 22.46\ldots$. Since $t$ counts whole toolboxes, the greatest number is $22$, giving $540+1430=1970$ pounds. Twenty-three would give $2035$ pounds.

questions.solution: Multiply both sides by $2$: $5-3x>2x-12$. Subtract $2x$ and $5$: $-5x>-17$. Divide by $-5$ and reverse the inequality: $x<\dfrac{17}{5}=3.4$. The greatest integer below $3.4$ is $3$. Checking, $x=3$ gives $-2>-3$, true, while $x=4$ gives $-3.5>-2$, false.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $-1\le \dfrac{4-x}{3}<5$?
questions.solution: Multiply all three parts by $3$: $-3\le 4-x<15$. Subtract $4$: $-7\le -x<11$. Multiply all three parts by $-1$, reversing both signs: $7\ge x>-11$. Written with the smaller value first this is $-11<x\le 7$. Testing $x=7$ gives $-1\le -1<5$, true, and $x=-11$ gives $5<5$, false.

distractors.B: multiplied by $-1$ without reversing the signs, so both endpoints kept the wrong sign
distractors.C: divided the outer parts by $3$ instead of multiplying by $3$

questions.stem: A food truck pays 240 dollars in daily costs plus 3.50 dollars for each meal it makes. Each meal sells for 9 dollars. What is the least number of meals the truck must sell in a day for its profit to be at least 400 dollars?
questions.solution: If $m$ meals are made and sold, profit is $9m-(240+3.5m)=5.5m-240$ dollars. Require $5.5m-240\ge 400$, so $5.5m\ge 640$ and $m\ge 116.36\ldots$. Since $m$ counts whole meals, the least number is $117$: profit is $5.5(117)-240=403.5$ dollars. With $116$ meals profit is $398$ dollars, below the target.

questions.stem: Which of the following points satisfies both $2x+y\le 8$ and $y>x-3$?
questions.solution: Test each point in both inequalities. For $(1,2)$: $2+2=4\le 8$ is true and $2>-2$ is true. For $(0,-3)$: $-3>-3$ is false. For $(4,2)$: $8+2=10\le 8$ is false. For $(5,-2)$: $10-2=8\le 8$ is true but $-2>2$ is false.

distractors.B: treated the second inequality as $y\ge x-3$, so a point on that boundary looked acceptable
distractors.C: checked only the second inequality and ignored the first
distractors.D: checked only the first inequality and ignored the second

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $\dfrac{7-2x}{3}\ge \dfrac{x-4}{2}$?
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by $6$: $2(7-2x)\ge 3(x-4)$, so $14-4x\ge 3x-12$. Add $4x$ and $12$: $26\ge 7x$, which is $x\le \dfrac{26}{7}$, about $3.71$. The greatest integer is $3$: the left side is $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and the right side is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$. For $x=4$ the sides are $-\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $0$, so the inequality fails.

questions.stem: In the $xy$-plane, a dashed line passes through $(0,4)$ with slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$, and the half-plane that does not contain the origin is shaded. Which inequality describes the shaded region?
questions.solution: The boundary is $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+4$. Multiplying by $2$ and rearranging gives $x+2y=8$. At the origin, $x+2y=0$, which is less than $8$, so the origin lies in the region where $x+2y<8$. The shaded region is the other side, $x+2y>8$, and the dashed boundary keeps the inequality strict.

distractors.A: shaded the side containing the origin instead of the side that excludes it
distractors.C: chose the correct side but treated the dashed boundary as solid
distractors.D: shaded the side containing the origin and also included the dashed boundary

questions.stem: A printer starts with 1,500 sheets of paper. Printing the cover pages uses 60 sheets in total, and each report uses 24 sheets. At least 200 sheets must be left afterward. What is the greatest number of reports that can be printed?
questions.solution: If $r$ reports are printed, the sheets left are $1500-60-24r=1440-24r$. Require $1440-24r\ge 200$. Subtract $1440$: $-24r\ge -1240$. Divide by $-24$ and reverse the inequality: $r\le 51.66\ldots$. The greatest whole number is $51$, leaving $1440-1224=216$ sheets. Printing $52$ reports would leave $192$ sheets.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes all values of $x$ for which $\dfrac{x}{3}-2>\dfrac{x}{2}+1$?
questions.solution: Multiply every term by $6$: $2x-12>3x+6$. Subtract $3x$ and add $12$: $-x>18$. Multiply by $-1$ and reverse the inequality: $x<-18$. Testing $x=-24$ gives $-10>-11$, true; testing $x=0$ gives $-2>1$, false.

questions.stem: What is the least integer value of $x$ that satisfies $5-\dfrac{3x}{4}\le \dfrac{x}{2}-3$?
questions.solution: Multiply every term by $4$: $20-3x\le 2x-12$. Subtract $2x$ and $20$: $-5x\le -32$. Divide by $-5$ and reverse the inequality: $x\ge \dfrac{32}{5}=6.4$. The least integer at or above $6.4$ is $7$: the left side is $-0.25$ and the right side is $0.5$. For $x=6$ the sides are $0.5$ and $0$, so the inequality fails.

questions.stem: A worker earns 18 dollars per hour for the first 40 hours of a week and 27 dollars for each hour beyond 40. She wants to earn at least 900 dollars in a week. Which inequality gives the possible numbers of hours $h$ beyond 40?
questions.solution: The first 40 hours pay $18(40)=720$ dollars, and the extra hours pay $27h$ dollars, so the week's earnings are $720+27h$. "At least 900 dollars" allows exactly $900$, so the symbol is $\ge$: $720+27h\ge 900$.

questions.stem: What is the greatest integer value of $x$ that satisfies $-2<\dfrac{6-x}{4}\le 3$?
questions.solution: Multiply all three parts by $4$: $-8<6-x\le 12$. Subtract $6$: $-14<-x\le 6$. Multiply all three parts by $-1$, reversing both signs: $14>x\ge -6$, that is $-6\le x<14$. Because $14$ is not allowed, the greatest integer is $13$, where $\dfrac{6-13}{4}=-1.75$ and $-2<-1.75\le 3$ holds.

questions.stem: A courier charges a flat fee of $6$ dollars for a delivery plus $2$ dollars for each mile driven. One delivery cost $26$ dollars. How many miles was that delivery?
questions.solution: Let $m$ be the number of miles. The flat fee is constant and the mileage charge is $2m$, so $6+2m=26$. Subtracting $6$ gives $2m=20$, so $m=10$ miles.

questions.stem: Five less than twice a number is $17$. What is the number?
questions.solution: Let the number be $n$. Twice the number is $2n$, and five less than that is $2n-5$, so $2n-5=17$. Adding $5$ gives $2n=22$, so $n=11$. Checking, $2(11)-5=17$.

questions.stem: A jacket is priced at $48$ dollars. A coupon takes $25$ percent off the price. What is the price after the coupon, in dollars?
questions.solution: The coupon removes $25$ percent of $48$, which is $0.25(48)=12$ dollars. The price paid is $48-12=36$ dollars. Equivalently, the shopper pays $75$ percent of the price: $0.75(48)=36$.

questions.solution: Let $t$ be the number of minutes. The amount in the tank is the starting $6$ gallons plus $4t$ gallons added, so $6+4t=50$. Subtracting $6$ gives $4t=44$, so $t=11$ minutes.
