questions.solution: Standard deviation measures how far the values typically sit from the mean. In $P$ the distances from $50$ are at most $2$; in $Q$ they run out to $20$. So $Q$ has the larger standard deviation.

distractors.B: chose the set whose values are closest together, reversing what spread measures
distractors.C: picked the right set for the wrong reason, judging spread from the largest value alone
distractors.D: treated equal means as meaning equal spread

questions.stem: A list of $7$ numbers has a mean of $12$. Every number in the list is increased by $5$. What is the mean of the new list?
questions.solution: Adding $5$ to each of the $7$ numbers adds $7(5)=35$ to the total, so the total rises from $84$ to $119$ and the new mean is $\dfrac{119}{7}=17$. Adding a constant to every value shifts the mean by that same constant: $12+5=17$.

questions.stem: The ordered list $4$, $6$, $9$, $10$, $16$ has median $9$. Every value in the list is multiplied by $3$. What is the median of the new list?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by $3$ gives $12$, $18$, $27$, $30$, $48$, still in order. The middle value is now $27$. Multiplying every value by a positive constant multiplies the median by that constant: $3(9)=27$.

distractors.A: thought multiplying every value leaves the median unchanged
distractors.B: added 3 to the median instead of multiplying by 3
distractors.D: tripled the largest value, 16, instead of the median

questions.stem: What is the range of the data set $7$, $-3$, $12$, $0$, $5$?
questions.solution: The largest value is $12$ and the smallest is $-3$. The range is $12-(-3)=12+3=15$.

distractors.A: dropped the minus sign and computed 12 minus 3
distractors.B: gave the largest value as the range
distractors.D: added the five values instead of subtracting the smallest from the largest

questions.stem: What is the mean of the five numbers $-6$, $-2$, $0$, $4$ and $9$?
questions.solution: Add with the signs: $-6+(-2)+0+4+9=5$. Divide by the $5$ values: $\dfrac{5}{5}=1$.

distractors.A: gave the median of the ordered list instead of the mean
distractors.C: left the 0 out of the count and divided 5 by 4
distractors.D: dropped both minus signs, totalling 21 and dividing by 5

questions.stem: Eleven students were asked how many pets they own. One pet was reported by $5$ students, two pets by $4$ students, and three pets by $2$ students. What is the median number of pets?
questions.solution: There are $11$ responses, so the median is the $6$th one when they are listed in order. The first $5$ responses are $1$ pet, and responses $6$ through $9$ are $2$ pets. The $6$th response is $2$, so the median is $2$ pets.

distractors.A: gave the most common value, the mode, instead of the median
distractors.C: reported the frequency of the middle group rather than the value
distractors.D: gave the position of the middle response, the 6th, instead of the value there

questions.stem: A basketball player averaged $14$ points per game over $6$ games. How many points did she score in total?
questions.solution: The mean per game times the number of games gives the total: $14\times 6=84$ points.

distractors.A: subtracted 6 from 14 instead of multiplying
distractors.B: added 6 to 14 instead of multiplying
distractors.D: multiplied 14 by 10 instead of by 6

questions.stem: A shop records the sizes of the shoes it sold: size $7$ sold $3$ times, size $8$ sold $6$ times, size $9$ sold $4$ times, and size $10$ sold $2$ times. What is the mode of the shoe sizes sold?
questions.solution: The mode is the size that occurs most often. Size $8$ was sold $6$ times, more than any other size, so the mode is $8$.

questions.stem: The data set $4$, $5$, $6$, $7$, $48$ has a mean of $14$. The value $48$ is removed. What is the mean of the four values that remain?
questions.solution: The original total is $70$. Removing $48$ leaves a total of $70-48=22$ spread over $4$ values, so the new mean is $\dfrac{22}{4}=5.5$. Taking out the one extreme value pulls the mean down sharply.

distractors.A: subtracted 48 from the total but still divided by 5
distractors.C: assumed removing a value leaves the mean unchanged
distractors.D: divided the original total of 70 by 4 without removing 48 from it

questions.stem: The mean of the five numbers $-8$, $3$, $x$, $7$ and $-2$ is $2$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: A mean of $2$ over $5$ numbers means the total is $5(2)=10$. The four known values total $-8+3+7+(-2)=0$, so $x=10-0=10$.

distractors.A: reversed the subtraction, computing 0 minus 10 instead of 10 minus 0
distractors.B: found the total of the four known values and stopped there
distractors.C: assumed the missing value must equal the mean

questions.stem: A list of $9$ numbers has a mean of $6$. A tenth number, $15$, is added to the list. What is the mean of the $10$ numbers?
questions.solution: The original total is $9(6)=54$. Adding $15$ makes the total $69$ over $10$ numbers, so the new mean is $\dfrac{69}{10}=6.9$.

questions.stem: The four numbers $5$, $8$, $x$ and $14$ have a median of $10$, and $x$ is between $8$ and $14$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: Since $x$ lies between $8$ and $14$, the ordered list is $5$, $8$, $x$, $14$. The median of four values is the mean of the middle two: $\dfrac{8+x}{2}=10$, so $8+x=20$ and $x=12$.

distractors.A: assumed the unknown value must equal the median itself
distractors.B: averaged 8 and 14 instead of solving for x
distractors.D: doubled the median but forgot to subtract the 8

questions.stem: Four of a student's five quiz scores are $82$, $76$, $91$ and $68$. The mean of all five scores is $80$. What is the fifth score?
questions.solution: A mean of $80$ over $5$ scores means the total is $5(80)=400$. The four known scores total $82+76+91+68=317$, so the fifth score is $400-317=83$.

questions.stem: The ordered list $11$, $13$, $15$, $17$, $19$ has mean $15$ and median $15$. The value $19$ is changed to $59$. Which statement about the new list is true?
choices: The mean increases by $8$ and the median does not change.
Both the mean and the median increase by $8$.
The median increases by $8$ and the mean does not change.
The mean and the median both increase by $40$.
questions.solution: The new total is $11+13+15+17+59=115$, so the new mean is $\dfrac{115}{5}=23$, which is $8$ more than $15$. The ordered list is now $11$, $13$, $15$, $17$, $59$, so the middle value is still $15$ and the median does not move.

distractors.B: assumed the median follows the mean whenever a value changes
distractors.C: swapped the roles of the mean and the median
distractors.D: applied the whole increase of 40 to both measures instead of sharing it over 5 values

questions.stem: A quiz was marked out of $5$. The score $2$ was earned $3$ times, the score $3$ was earned $5$ times, the score $4$ was earned $6$ times, and the score $5$ was earned $2$ times. What is the median score?
questions.solution: There are $3+5+6+2=16$ scores, so the median is the mean of the $8$th and $9$th scores in order. The first $3$ are $2$s and scores $4$ through $8$ are $3$s, so the $8$th is $3$; scores $9$ through $14$ are $4$s, so the $9$th is $4$. The median is $\dfrac{3+4}{2}=3.5$.

questions.stem: A teacher records days absent for $20$ students: $8$ students missed $0$ days, $6$ missed $1$ day, $4$ missed $2$ days, and $2$ missed $5$ days. What is the mean number of days absent?
questions.solution: The total days missed are $8(0)+6(1)+4(2)+2(5)=0+6+8+10=24$. Dividing by the $20$ students gives $\dfrac{24}{20}=1.2$ days.

distractors.A: found the median number of days absent instead of the mean
distractors.C: averaged the four different values, (0+1+2+5)/4, ignoring how many students had each
distractors.D: divided the total of 24 by the 4 different values instead of by 20 students

questions.stem: Two classes of $20$ students each have the same mean test score, $78$. In class A nearly every score lies between $74$ and $82$. In class B many scores are below $60$ and many are above $95$. Which statement is true?
choices: The two classes have the same mean, but class B has the greater standard deviation.
Class A has the greater standard deviation, because its scores are packed close together.
Class B has the greater mean, because it contains the highest scores.
The standard deviations are equal, because the means are equal.
questions.solution: Both classes are stated to have mean $78$, so the centres match. Standard deviation measures typical distance from the mean: class A's scores sit within about $4$ points of $78$, while class B's sit tens of points away on both sides. Class B therefore has the greater standard deviation.

distractors.B: treated tightly packed data as having the larger spread
distractors.C: judged the centre from the largest values rather than from the stated mean
distractors.D: treated equal means as forcing equal spread

questions.stem: A list of $12$ numbers has a median of $23$ and a range of $8$. Every number in the list is decreased by $7$. What are the median and the range of the new list?
choices: The median is $16$ and the range is $1$.
The median is $23$ and the range is $8$.
The median is $16$ and the range is $15$.
The median is $16$ and the range is $8$.
questions.solution: Subtracting $7$ from every value slides the whole list down by $7$, so the median drops to $23-7=16$. The largest and smallest values both drop by $7$ as well, so their difference is unchanged and the range stays $8$.

distractors.A: subtracted 7 from the range as well as from the median
distractors.B: left the median unchanged, as the range is
distractors.C: added 7 to the range instead of leaving it alone

questions.stem: A data set has a mean of $14$ and a range of $9$. Every value in the data set is multiplied by $2$. What are the mean and the range of the new data set?
choices: The mean is $16$ and the range is $11$.
The mean is $28$ and the range is $9$.
The mean is $14$ and the range is $18$.
The mean is $28$ and the range is $18$.
questions.solution: Doubling every value doubles the total, so the mean doubles to $2(14)=28$. The largest and smallest values also double, so their difference doubles: the range becomes $2(9)=18$.

distractors.A: added 2 to each measure instead of multiplying by 2
distractors.B: doubled the mean but assumed the range is unaffected
distractors.C: doubled the range but assumed the mean is unaffected

questions.stem: The ordered list $30$, $34$, $36$, $36$, $40$, $44$, $48$ has a median of $36$. The value $300$ is added to the list. What is the median of the eight values?
questions.solution: In order the new list is $30$, $34$, $36$, $36$, $40$, $44$, $48$, $300$. With $8$ values the median is the mean of the $4$th and $5$th: $\dfrac{36+40}{2}=38$. The extreme value nudges the median up by only $2$.

distractors.A: assumed adding one value cannot change the median at all
distractors.C: took the 5th value alone as the middle of an eight-value list
distractors.D: found the new mean, 568 divided by 8, instead of the new median

questions.stem: A list of $6$ numbers has a mean of $9$. One of the numbers, $4$, is removed from the list. What is the mean of the remaining $5$ numbers?
questions.solution: The original total is $6(9)=54$. Removing $4$ leaves a total of $50$ over $5$ numbers, so the new mean is $\dfrac{50}{5}=10$. Taking away a value below the mean pulls the mean up.

questions.stem: In the ordered list $2$, $4$, $5$, $9$, $12$, $14$, $15$, the largest value $15$ is replaced by $150$. Which measure of the data set is unchanged?
choices: The mean, the median and the range all change.
questions.solution: With $7$ values the median is the $4$th, which is $9$; the replacement keeps $150$ at the end of the ordered list, so the $4$th value is still $9$. The total rises by $135$, so the mean changes, and the range rises from $15-2=13$ to $150-2=148$.

distractors.B: thought an extreme replacement leaves the mean alone
distractors.C: thought the range depends only on the smallest value
distractors.D: assumed every measure must react when a value changes

questions.stem: A class of $10$ students has a mean score of $80$. A second class of $15$ students has a mean score of $70$. What is the mean score of all $25$ students?
questions.solution: Turn each mean into a total: $10(80)=800$ and $15(70)=1050$. Together that is $1850$ points over $25$ students, so the mean is $\dfrac{1850}{25}=74$.

distractors.B: averaged the two means without weighting them by class size
distractors.C: paired each mean with the other class's size, giving (15(80)+10(70))/25
distractors.D: added the two means instead of combining the totals

questions.stem: The numbers $-5$, $12$, $-1$, $8$, $3$, $0$, $-9$ are not in order. What is the median of this data set?
questions.solution: In increasing order the values are $-9$, $-5$, $-1$, $0$, $3$, $8$, $12$. There are $7$ values, so the median is the $4$th one, which is $0$.

questions.stem: In a small office, eight employees earn between $40$ and $55$ thousand dollars a year, and the owner earns $600$ thousand dollars a year. Which statement about these nine salaries is true?
choices: The median is greater than the mean, so the mean better represents a typical salary.
The mean and the median are equal because there are nine salaries.
The mean better represents a typical salary, because it takes every salary into account.
The mean is greater than the median, and the median better represents a typical salary.
questions.solution: The owner's salary alone adds over $60$ thousand dollars to the mean, pushing the mean above every employee's salary, so the mean exceeds the median. The median is the $5$th salary in order, which sits among the eight similar ones, so it describes a typical salary far better.

distractors.A: got the direction of the skew backwards, as one very large value lifts the mean above the median
distractors.B: thought an odd number of values forces the mean and median to agree
distractors.C: chose the mean because it uses every value, overlooking that one extreme salary distorts it

questions.stem: In a data set the value $2$ occurs $4$ times and the value $5$ occurs $k$ times, and no other values occur. The mean of the data set is $4$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: The total is $4(2)+5k=8+5k$ and the count is $4+k$, so $\dfrac{8+5k}{4+k}=4$. Then $8+5k=4(4+k)=16+4k$, giving $k=8$.

distractors.A: did not distribute, writing 4(4+k) as 16+k
distractors.B: assumed the two values must occur equally often
distractors.D: found the total number of values, 4 plus 8, instead of k

questions.stem: A set of $8$ numbers has a mean of $12$. One of the numbers, $7$, is replaced by $31$. What is the mean of the new set?
questions.solution: The original total is $8(12)=96$. Replacing $7$ by $31$ changes the total by $31-7=24$, making it $120$. There are still $8$ numbers, so the new mean is $\dfrac{120}{8}=15$.

questions.stem: Set $X$ is $12$, $14$, $15$, $16$, $18$ and set $Y$ is $5$, $9$, $15$, $21$, $25$. Both lists are in order. Which statement is true?
choices: Set $Y$ has the greater mean, because it contains larger values.
The two sets have the same mean and the same median, but set $Y$ has the greater standard deviation.
Set $X$ has the greater standard deviation, because more of its values are near $15$.
The two sets have the same standard deviation, because they have the same mean.
questions.solution: Each set totals $75$ over $5$ values, so both means are $15$, and the middle value of each ordered list is $15$, so both medians are $15$. The values of $X$ stay within $3$ of $15$, while those of $Y$ reach $10$ away, so $Y$ is the more spread out set and has the greater standard deviation.

distractors.A: judged the mean from the largest values rather than computing the totals
distractors.C: treated values clustered near the mean as producing the larger spread
distractors.D: treated equal means as forcing equal spread

questions.stem: A list of $7$ numbers has a mean of $20$. One more number is added so that the mean of the $8$ numbers is $22$. What number was added?
questions.solution: The original total is $7(20)=140$ and the required new total is $8(22)=176$. The added number is $176-140=36$.

distractors.A: gave the increase in the mean instead of the added number
distractors.B: added a number equal to the new mean
distractors.C: added the increase of 2 to the new mean of 22

questions.stem: The ordered list $8$, $11$, $14$, $17$, $20$, $23$ has a mean of $15.5$. A seventh value is added and the mean of the seven values is $16$. What is the median of the seven values?
questions.solution: The six values total $93$. Seven values with mean $16$ total $7(16)=112$, so the added value is $112-93=19$. In order the list is $8$, $11$, $14$, $17$, $19$, $20$, $23$, and the median is the $4$th value, $17$.

distractors.A: carried the old mean through as the answer
distractors.B: reported the new mean as though it were the median
distractors.D: gave the value that was added instead of the median

questions.stem: A list of $5$ numbers has a mean of $11$ and a median of $9$. The two largest numbers in the list are $14$ and $18$. What is the sum of the two smallest numbers?
questions.solution: The total of the five numbers is $5(11)=55$. The median of five numbers is the middle one, so one of them is $9$, and the two largest are $14$ and $18$. Those three total $9+14+18=41$, so the two smallest sum to $55-41=14$.

questions.stem: A data set of $6$ values has a mean of $9$. Every value is multiplied by $3$ and then $4$ is subtracted from each result. What is the mean of the new data set?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by $3$ multiplies the mean by $3$, giving $27$. Subtracting $4$ from every value lowers the mean by $4$, giving $27-4=23$. Checking with totals: the original total is $54$, the new total is $3(54)-6(4)=162-24=138$, and $\dfrac{138}{6}=23$.

distractors.A: subtracted 4 from the mean and forgot to multiply by 3
distractors.B: applied the steps in the wrong order, computing (9-4) times 3
distractors.D: multiplied by 3 and forgot to subtract 4

questions.stem: A data set of $20$ values contains only two different values: $4$ occurs $12$ times and $x$ occurs $8$ times. The mean of the data set is $6$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution: A mean of $6$ over $20$ values means the total is $20(6)=120$. The twelve $4$s contribute $48$, so the eight copies of $x$ contribute $120-48=72$. Then $8x=72$, so $x=9$.

questions.stem: The ages of $22$ children are recorded: age $12$ occurs $5$ times, age $13$ occurs $6$ times, age $14$ occurs $7$ times, and age $15$ occurs $4$ times. What is the median age?
questions.solution: With $22$ values the median is the mean of the $11$th and $12$th ages in order. Positions $1$ through $5$ are age $12$ and positions $6$ through $11$ are age $13$, so the $11$th is $13$; positions $12$ through $18$ are age $14$, so the $12$th is $14$. The median is $\dfrac{13+14}{2}=13.5$.

distractors.A: averaged the two middle positions, 11 and 12, instead of the values at those positions
distractors.B: stopped at the 11th value instead of averaging the two middle values
distractors.D: gave the most common age, the mode, instead of the median

questions.stem: Two lists each contain $6$ values and each has a mean of $30$. The first list has a standard deviation of $2$ and the second has a standard deviation of $11$. Which statement must be true?
choices: On the whole, the values in the second list lie farther from $30$ than the values in the first list.
The second list has a larger mean than the first list.
Every value in the second list is larger than every value in the first list.
The second list contains more values than the first list.
questions.solution: Standard deviation describes typical distance from the mean, not the mean itself and not the number of values. Both lists have mean $30$ and six values, so the only difference the larger standard deviation records is that the second list's values sit farther from $30$, on both sides of it.

distractors.B: read a larger standard deviation as a larger centre
distractors.C: treated greater spread as meaning every value is larger
distractors.D: treated greater spread as meaning more data points

questions.stem: A list of $8$ numbers has a mean of $17$. One number is removed and the remaining $7$ numbers have a mean of $18$. What number was removed?
questions.solution: The original total is $8(17)=136$ and the remaining total is $7(18)=126$. The number removed is $136-126=10$. It is below the old mean, which is why removing it raised the mean.

questions.stem: The ordered list $5$, $6$, $8$, $9$, $12$ has mean $8$ and median $8$. The value $12$ is replaced by $42$, and then every value in the resulting list is increased by $3$. What are the mean and the median of the final list?
choices: The mean is $11$ and the median is $11$.
The mean is $17$ and the median is $8$.
The mean is $14$ and the median is $11$.
The mean is $17$ and the median is $11$.
questions.solution: After the replacement the list is $5$, $6$, $8$, $9$, $42$, with total $70$, so the mean is $14$; the middle value is still $8$, so the median is $8$. Adding $3$ to every value raises both measures by $3$: the mean becomes $17$ and the median becomes $11$.

distractors.A: added 3 to the old mean of 8 without accounting for the replaced value
distractors.B: forgot to add 3 to the median
distractors.C: forgot to add 3 to the mean

questions.stem: The ordered list $4$, $7$, $9$, $11$, $20$ has a median of $9$. Which one of these changes leaves the median equal to $9$?
choices: Adding the value $2$ to the list
questions.solution: Replacing $20$ with $100$ gives $4$, $7$, $9$, $11$, $100$, whose middle value is still $9$. The others move it: $4$ becoming $10$ reorders the list to $7$, $9$, $10$, $11$, $20$ with median $10$; changing the $9$ itself to $15$ gives $4$, $7$, $11$, $15$, $20$ with median $11$; adding $2$ makes six values, $2$, $4$, $7$, $9$, $11$, $20$, with median $\dfrac{7+9}{2}=8$.

distractors.A: did not re-sort after the change, missing that 10 moves past 9 and the median becomes 10
distractors.B: changed the middle value itself, which moves the median to 11
distractors.C: overlooked that a sixth value makes the median the average of 7 and 9, which is 8

questions.stem: A list of $10$ numbers has a mean of $15$. The two numbers $7$ and $3$ are removed from the list. What is the mean of the remaining $8$ numbers?
questions.solution: The original total is $10(15)=150$. Removing $7$ and $3$ takes away $10$, leaving a total of $140$ over $8$ numbers, so the new mean is $\dfrac{140}{8}=17.5$. Both removed numbers were below the old mean, so the mean rose.

distractors.A: subtracted 10 from the total but still divided by 10
distractors.B: assumed removing values leaves the mean unchanged
distractors.D: divided the original total of 150 by 8 without removing the two values

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A researcher records the number of hours $x$ that a plant is exposed to light each day and its height $y$ in centimetres. The line of best fit is $y = 1.4x + 6$. What does the number $1.4$ represent?
choices: the predicted height of a plant that gets no light
the predicted extra hours of light needed for each extra centimetre of height
the total height of the plant
the predicted increase in height, in centimetres, for each additional hour of light
questions.solution: In $y = mx + b$ the slope $m$ is the predicted change in $y$ for a one-unit rise in $x$. Here $x$ is hours of light and $y$ is height in centimetres, so a slope of $1.4$ means each additional hour of light predicts $1.4$ more centimetres of height.

distractors.A: gave the meaning of the constant 6 (height at zero light) instead of the slope
distractors.B: swapped x and y, reading the slope as hours per centimetre
distractors.C: treated the slope as a height rather than a rate of change

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A tutor fits the line of best fit $y = 6x + 42$, where $x$ is the number of hours a student studied and $y$ is the test score. The data covers study times from $1$ to $10$ hours. What score does the line predict for a student who studies $7$ hours?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 7$ into the line: $y = 6(7) + 42 = 42 + 42 = 84$. Since $7$ hours lies inside the range of the data, this prediction is reasonable.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A gym fits the line of best fit $y = 3.5x + 20$, where $x$ is the number of weeks a member has trained and $y$ is the number of minutes the member can run without stopping. What does the number $20$ represent?
choices: the predicted minutes a member can run after one week of training
the increase in minutes for each extra week of training
the number of weeks needed to run for 20 minutes
the predicted minutes a member can run at week 0, before any training
questions.solution: The constant term is the value of $y$ when $x = 0$. Putting $x = 0$ gives $y = 3.5(0) + 20 = 20$, so the model predicts a member can run for $20$ minutes before any weeks of training.

distractors.A: used x = 1 instead of x = 0, so read the constant as the week-1 value
distractors.B: read the constant term as the slope
distractors.C: swapped the roles of x and y

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A scatterplot shows the age of a used car on the horizontal axis and its price on the vertical axis. The points fall steadily from left to right and lie close to a straight line. Which best describes the association between age and price?
questions.solution: Points falling from left to right mean that as age increases, price decreases, which is a negative association. Because the points lie close to a straight line, the association is strong.

distractors.A: read falling points as a positive association
distractors.B: read falling points as positive and the tight pattern as weak
distractors.D: assumed that a decreasing pattern means there is no association

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(2, 11)$ and $(6, 23)$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: The slope is the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$: $\dfrac{23-11}{6-2} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: Over twelve months a town records the number of ice cream cones sold each month and the number of sunburns reported each month. The two are strongly positively associated. Which conclusion is supported by this information?
choices: Sunburn causes people to buy ice cream.
Months with more cones sold tend to be months with more sunburns reported.
Reducing ice cream sales would reduce the number of sunburns.
questions.solution: An association says only that the two quantities tend to move together. Here hot, sunny months raise both figures. The data supports a statement about the pattern, not a statement that one quantity causes the other.

distractors.A: treated an association as proof of causation
distractors.B: treated the association as causation running the other way
distractors.D: assumed that changing one variable would change the other

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: For a set of data, the line of best fit is $y = 4x + 9$. One of the data points is $(5, 32)$. How does the actual value at $x = 5$ compare with the value the line predicts?
questions.solution: The line predicts $y = 4(5) + 9 = 29$ at $x = 5$. The actual value is $32$, and $32 - 29 = 3$, so the actual value is $3$ greater than the predicted value.

distractors.A: subtracted in the wrong order, giving 29 - 32
distractors.C: used the x-value 5 as the size of the difference
distractors.D: assumed every data point lies exactly on the line of best fit

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A shop models the stock left during a sale with the line of best fit $y = -2x + 50$, where $x$ is the number of days since the sale began and $y$ is the number of items left. How many items does the line predict are left after $12$ days?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 12$: $y = -2(12) + 50$. First $-2(12) = -24$, then $-24 + 50 = 26$. The model predicts $26$ items are left. Keeping the negative sign on $-24$ matters here.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A colony of bacteria doubles in size every hour. Which type of model best describes the relationship between the number of hours and the size of the colony?
choices: Linear, because the same number of bacteria is added each hour.
Exponential, because the size is multiplied by the same factor each hour.
Linear, because the colony decreases steadily.
Exponential, because the colony is halved each hour.
questions.solution: Doubling means multiplying by $2$ each hour, so the colony is multiplied by a constant factor over equal time steps. A constant ratio gives an exponential model; a linear model needs a constant amount added instead.

distractors.A: treated a constant ratio as a constant amount added, giving a linear model
distractors.C: described the colony as shrinking when doubling makes it grow
distractors.D: used a factor of one half instead of 2, describing decay rather than growth

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: In a study of adults, the line of best fit is $y = 0.4x + 15$, where $x$ is height in centimetres and $y$ is forearm length in centimetres. The heights in the data run from $150$ to $195$ centimetres. Why is the value $15$ not meaningful in this context?
choices: It would be the predicted forearm length of an adult who is 0 centimetres tall, which no adult is.
It would be the predicted height of an adult whose forearm is 0 centimetres long.
It is the increase in forearm length for each extra centimetre of height.
It cannot be meaningful because the slope is less than 1.
questions.solution: The constant term is the predicted $y$ when $x = 0$, that is, the forearm length of an adult of height $0$ centimetres. No such adult exists, and $x = 0$ is far outside the data range of $150$ to $195$, so the number has no real meaning here.

distractors.B: swapped x and y when reading the constant term
distractors.C: read the constant term as the slope
distractors.D: thought a slope below 1 makes a model invalid

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 7x + 5$. At $x = 4$ one of the observed data values is $y = 30$. By how much is the observed value below the value the line predicts?
questions.solution: The predicted value is $y = 7(4) + 5 = 28 + 5 = 33$. The observed value is $30$, and $33 - 30 = 3$, so the observed value is $3$ below the prediction.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A scatterplot shows each student's shoe size on the horizontal axis and the student's score on a history quiz on the vertical axis. The points are spread out with no upward or downward trend. Which best describes the association?
questions.solution: An association means the points show a trend in one direction. Here the points show neither a rise nor a fall as shoe size increases, so there is no association between shoe size and quiz score.

distractors.A: assumed every scatterplot shows an upward trend
distractors.B: assumed every scatterplot must show a trend and read the scatter as downward
distractors.C: mistook random scatter for a slight upward trend

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A delivery company models its charges with the line of best fit $y = 1.8x + 4$, where $x$ is the distance in miles and $y$ is the cost in dollars. According to the model, what is the extra cost, in dollars, for each additional mile?
questions.solution: The slope is the predicted change in $y$ for a one-unit rise in $x$. Here the slope is $1.8$, so each additional mile predicts an extra cost of $1.80$ dollars. The constant $4$ is the cost before any distance is travelled.

distractors.B: subtracted the rate from the fixed charge, 4 - 1.8
distractors.C: gave the fixed starting charge instead of the rate per mile
distractors.D: added the fixed charge and the rate, 4 + 1.8

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit has slope $4$ and passes through the point $(3, 20)$. What is the $y$-intercept of the line?
questions.solution: Write $y = 4x + b$ and substitute the point: $20 = 4(3) + b = 12 + b$, so $b = 20 - 12 = 8$. The $y$-intercept is $8$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A study reports that students who own more books tend to score higher on reading tests. A newspaper prints the headline "Buying books raises reading scores." What is the main problem with the headline?
choices: The association described is negative, not positive.
Higher reading scores cause students to own more books, so the headline is backwards.
An association between two quantities does not show that one causes the other.
Reading scores cannot be measured reliably.
questions.solution: The study observed a pattern: book ownership and reading scores rise together. Something else, such as how much reading happens at home, could raise both. Observed association alone does not establish that buying books causes the higher scores.

distractors.A: misread the direction of the reported association
distractors.B: accepted causation and merely turned it around
distractors.D: raised a measurement objection the study does not support

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A coach uses the line of best fit $y = 5x + 30$, where $x$ is the number of practice sessions and $y$ is the number of points scored in a season. The data covers $2$ to $15$ sessions. What does the line predict for a player with $9$ sessions?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 9$: $y = 5(9) + 30 = 45 + 30 = 75$. The model predicts $75$ points, and $9$ sessions lies inside the data range of $2$ to $15$.

distractors.A: added 9 to 30 and never multiplied by 5
distractors.B: computed 5 times 9 and dropped the constant 30
distractors.D: added before multiplying, computing 5(9 + 30)

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 0.5x + 3$. For what value of $x$ does the line predict that $y = 10$?
questions.solution: Set $0.5x + 3 = 10$. Subtracting $3$ from both sides gives $0.5x = 7$, and dividing by $0.5$ gives $x = 14$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit $y = 2x + 40$ models $y$, a child's height in centimetres, against $x$, the child's age in years. The data comes from children aged $5$ to $12$. Why should this line not be used to predict the height of a $40$-year-old?
choices: An age of 40 is far outside the range of the data, so the pattern may not continue there.
The slope of the line is too small for a prediction.
The constant term of the line is positive.
Height can never be predicted from age.
questions.solution: The line describes only the ages the data covers, $5$ to $12$. Predicting at $x = 40$ is extrapolation far beyond that range. Growth in height does not continue at $2$ centimetres per year into adulthood, so the prediction is unreliable.

distractors.B: thought the size of the slope decides whether a prediction is valid
distractors.C: thought a positive constant term makes a model unusable
distractors.D: ruled out all predictions instead of identifying extrapolation

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A savings account holds $500$ dollars and grows by $3$ percent of its current balance each year. Which model best describes the balance over time?
choices: Linear, because the same number of dollars is added each year.
Exponential, because the balance is multiplied by 1.03 each year.
Linear, because 3 percent is a fixed figure.
Exponential, because the balance is multiplied by 0.03 each year.
questions.solution: Growing by $3$ percent of the current balance means multiplying by $1.03$ each year, a constant factor, so the model is exponential. The dollar amount added grows each year because the balance it is taken from grows.

distractors.A: treated a constant percent as a constant dollar amount
distractors.C: treated the fixed percentage as a fixed amount added each year
distractors.D: used 0.03 as the multiplier instead of 1.03, which would shrink the balance

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A health programme uses the line of best fit $y = -4x + 60$, where $x$ is the number of weeks in the programme and $y$ is a participant's weight in kilograms. What does the number $-4$ mean?
choices: The model predicts a loss of 4 kilograms for each extra week in the programme.
The starting weight of a participant is 4 kilograms.
The model predicts a gain of 4 kilograms for each extra week in the programme.
It takes 4 weeks to lose 1 kilogram.
questions.solution: The slope is the predicted change in $y$ for a one-unit rise in $x$. A slope of $-4$ means $y$ falls by $4$ when $x$ rises by $1$, so the model predicts a loss of $4$ kilograms for each extra week. The negative sign carries the meaning here.

distractors.B: read the slope as the starting value, which is the constant 60
distractors.C: dropped the negative sign and read a decrease as an increase
distractors.D: swapped x and y, inverting the rate

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A city models bus use with the line of best fit $y = -0.8x + 46$, where $x$ is the number of years since 2010 and $y$ is the number of daily riders in thousands. The data covers 2010 through 2022. Which statement is best supported?
choices: Daily ridership fell by about 800 riders per year.
Daily ridership fell by about 0.8 riders per year.
Daily ridership rose by about 800 riders per year.
There were 46 riders per day in 2010.
questions.solution: The slope is $-0.8$ in thousands of riders per year, and $0.8$ thousand is $800$. The negative sign means a fall, so ridership dropped by about $800$ riders per year.

distractors.B: ignored that y is measured in thousands
distractors.C: dropped the negative sign and described a rise
distractors.D: read the constant as a count of riders instead of thousands of riders

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A painter uses the line of best fit $y = 12x + 55$, where $x$ is the number of coats of paint and $y$ is the drying time in minutes. For one job with $6$ coats the observed drying time was $120$ minutes. By how many minutes does the predicted time exceed the observed time?
questions.solution: The predicted time is $y = 12(6) + 55 = 72 + 55 = 127$ minutes. The observed time was $120$ minutes, so the prediction exceeds the observation by $127 - 120 = 7$ minutes.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit $y = 3.2x + 18$ was built from data in which $x$, the number of minutes of exercise, ranges from $10$ to $45$. For which value of $x$ is a prediction from this line most reliable?
questions.solution: A prediction is most trustworthy when the input lies inside the range of the data, which here is $10$ to $45$. Only $25$ lies inside that range; $5$ is below it and $60$ and $120$ are above it.

distractors.A: chose a value below the range of the data
distractors.C: chose a value just above the range, assuming any nearby value is safe
distractors.D: chose a value far beyond the range of the data

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A factory uses the line of best fit $y = 9x + 150$, where $x$ is the number of extra machines running and $y$ is the daily output in units. What does the number $150$ represent?
choices: the predicted daily output for each extra machine
the number of extra machines needed to make 150 units
the predicted daily output when 9 extra machines are running
the predicted daily output when no extra machines are running
questions.solution: Setting $x = 0$ gives $y = 9(0) + 150 = 150$. So $150$ units is the output the model predicts when no extra machines are running. The slope $9$ is the extra output per extra machine.

distractors.A: read the constant term as the rate per machine
distractors.B: swapped the roles of x and y
distractors.C: treated the slope 9 as a number of machines and attached the constant to it

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(3, 17)$ and $(8, 42)$. What value does the line predict when $x = 10$?
questions.solution: The slope is $\dfrac{42-17}{8-3} = \dfrac{25}{5} = 5$. From $(8, 42)$, moving $2$ units right adds $2(5) = 10$, so at $x = 10$ the predicted value is $42 + 10 = 52$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: In a large town, the number of firefighters sent to a fire and the amount of damage the fire causes are strongly positively associated. Which explanation of this pattern is most reasonable?
choices: Sending more firefighters causes more damage.
There is no real association between the two quantities.
The pattern is a coincidence that cannot be explained.
Larger fires lead to both more firefighters being sent and more damage.
questions.solution: The size of the fire affects both quantities: a bigger fire draws more firefighters and also causes more damage. A third variable explains the association, so neither quantity need cause the other.

distractors.A: treated the association as direct causation
distractors.B: denied an association that the data shows
distractors.C: dismissed the pattern instead of looking for a variable affecting both

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: For a set of data the line of best fit is $y = -1.5x + 40$. One of the data points is $(8, 25)$. Which statement about this point is true?
choices: The observed value is 3 less than the predicted value.
The observed value is 3 greater than the predicted value.
The observed value is 15 less than the predicted value.
The observed value equals the predicted value.
questions.solution: At $x = 8$ the line predicts $y = -1.5(8) + 40 = -12 + 40 = 28$. The observed value is $25$, and $28 - 25 = 3$, so the observed value is $3$ below the prediction.

distractors.B: subtracted in the wrong order, giving 25 - 28 as a gain
distractors.C: compared the observed value with the constant 40 rather than the prediction 28
distractors.D: assumed every data point lies on the line of best fit

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit predicts a value of $32$ when $x = 4$ and a value of $56$ when $x = 10$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: Both described values lie on the line, so the slope is $\dfrac{56-32}{10-4} = \dfrac{24}{6} = 4$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: Two scatterplots are described. In plot P the points lie very close to a rising straight line. In plot Q the points rise overall but are widely spread out. Which statement is true?
choices: Both plots show a negative association, and P is the stronger one.
Both plots show a positive association, and P is the stronger one.
Both plots show a positive association, and Q is the stronger one.
P shows a positive association and Q shows no association.
questions.solution: Rising points mean a positive association in both plots. Strength depends on how closely the points cluster about a line, so P, with little scatter, shows the stronger association.

distractors.A: called a rising pattern negative
distractors.C: treated wide scatter as a sign of a stronger association
distractors.D: treated an overall rise with wide scatter as no association at all

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit has slope $-2.5$ and passes through the point $(6, 25)$. What is the $y$-intercept of the line?
questions.solution: Write $y = -2.5x + b$ and substitute: $25 = -2.5(6) + b = -15 + b$. Adding $15$ to both sides gives $b = 40$. Note that $-2.5(6)$ is $-15$, not $15$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A car is worth $20000$ dollars when new and loses $15$ percent of its current value each year. Which model best describes the car's value over time?
choices: Linear, decreasing by a fixed number of dollars each year.
questions.solution: Losing $15$ percent of the current value leaves $85$ percent of it, so each year the value is multiplied by $0.85$. A constant multiplier over equal time steps is an exponential model, and because $0.85 < 1$ the value decays.

distractors.A: treated a constant percent loss as a constant dollar loss
distractors.B: used 1.15, modelling growth instead of a 15 percent loss
distractors.D: ignored that the value falls over time

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A researcher finds a strong negative association between the hours teenagers spend on social media and the hours they sleep. Which additional step would best support the claim that social media use causes less sleep?
choices: Collect more observational data from the same teenagers.
Compute the line of best fit more precisely.
Check that the association is strong enough.
Run a controlled experiment that assigns teenagers different amounts of social media time.
questions.solution: Observed association cannot separate cause from a third variable. Randomly assigning the amount of social media time and then comparing sleep removes other explanations, so an experiment is what supports a causal claim.

distractors.A: assumed more observational data can establish causation
distractors.B: assumed a better-fitting line establishes causation
distractors.C: assumed a strong association establishes causation

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A park service uses the line of best fit $y = 2.4x + 18$, where $x$ is the number of trees planted and $y$ is the number of birds counted. For what value of $x$ does the line predict $y = 60$?
questions.solution: Set $2.4x + 18 = 60$. Subtracting $18$ gives $2.4x = 42$, and dividing by $2.4$ gives $x = \dfrac{42}{2.4} = 17.5$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A reservoir is modelled by the line of best fit $y = 0.25x + 3$, where $x$ is the number of days since monitoring began and $y$ is the water depth in metres. By how many metres does the model predict the depth rises in one week?
questions.solution: The slope says the depth rises $0.25$ metres per day. One week is $7$ days, so the predicted rise is $7(0.25) = 1.75$ metres.

distractors.A: gave the daily rate without converting it to a week
distractors.C: gave the constant term instead of a change in depth
distractors.D: gave the number of days in a week instead of the change in depth

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit was built from data on houses between $900$ and $2400$ square feet. A buyer uses it to predict the price of a $7000$-square-foot house. What is the best reason to doubt that prediction?
choices: The line has a positive slope.
No houses anywhere near 7000 square feet were in the data, so the trend may not continue there.
House prices are never related to size.
A line of best fit has no constant term.
questions.solution: The model describes the pattern only across the sizes in the data, $900$ to $2400$ square feet. At $7000$ square feet the prediction is far outside that range, and nothing in the data shows the same straight-line pattern continues that far.

distractors.A: thought a positive slope limits what can be predicted
distractors.C: made a sweeping claim instead of pointing to the range of the data
distractors.D: assumed the model has no constant term

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: For a data set the line of best fit is $y = 8x - 5$. One of the data points is $(7, 60)$. By how much is the observed value greater than the predicted value?
questions.solution: The predicted value is $y = 8(7) - 5 = 56 - 5 = 51$. The observed value is $60$, so the observed value exceeds the prediction by $60 - 51 = 9$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A phone plan is modelled by $y = 0.07x + 25$, where $x$ is the number of gigabytes of data used in a month and $y$ is the monthly bill in dollars. Which statement describes the model correctly?
choices: The bill rises by 25 dollars for each gigabyte used.
The bill is 0.07 dollars when no data is used.
The bill starts at 25 dollars and rises by 0.07 dollars for each gigabyte used.
The bill is 25 dollars for each gigabyte used, plus 0.07 dollars.
questions.solution: The constant $25$ is the bill when $x = 0$, a fixed monthly charge. The slope $0.07$ is the predicted rise in the bill for each extra gigabyte, so the bill starts at $25$ dollars and grows by $0.07$ dollars per gigabyte.

distractors.A: read the constant term as the rate per gigabyte
distractors.B: read the slope as the bill with no data used
distractors.D: turned the fixed monthly charge into a per-gigabyte charge

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(2, 50)$ and $(10, 18)$. Which equation represents this line?

distractors.B: dropped the negative sign on the slope
distractors.C: used the y-value 50 as the constant term without adjusting for x = 2
distractors.D: computed the slope as the change in x over the change in y

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: At $x = 0$, $1$, $2$ and $3$ the values of $y$ are $5$, $10$, $20$ and $40$. The pattern is exponential. What value does the pattern give at $x = 5$?
questions.solution: Each step multiplies $y$ by $2$, so the model is exponential with factor $2$. From $40$ at $x = 3$: at $x = 4$ the value is $80$, and at $x = 5$ it is $160$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: For which situation is a linear model more appropriate than an exponential model?
choices: A bank balance that earns 5 percent interest on its current value each year.
A tank that is filled at a steady rate of 4 litres per minute.
A population of fish that doubles every decade.
A sample of a substance that halves every six years.
questions.solution: A linear model fits a constant amount added per unit of time. Filling at $4$ litres per minute adds the same $4$ litres each minute. The other three describe multiplying by a constant factor, which is exponential.

distractors.A: treated compound percent growth as a constant amount added
distractors.C: treated repeated doubling as a constant amount added
distractors.D: treated repeated halving as a constant amount subtracted

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A study of towns uses the line of best fit $y = 0.0025x + 1.5$, where $x$ is the number of residents and $y$ is the number of doctors. According to the model, about how many additional residents correspond to one additional doctor?
questions.solution: Each extra resident predicts $0.0025$ more doctors. To gain one whole doctor, the number of extra residents needed is $\dfrac{1}{0.0025} = \dfrac{10000}{25} = 400$.

distractors.A: multiplied by the slope instead of dividing 1 by it
distractors.B: divided 1 by 0.25, moving the decimal two places too far
distractors.C: divided 1 by 0.025, moving the decimal one place too far

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: For a data set the line of best fit is $y = -3.5x + 92$. One of the data points is $(14, 50)$. By how much does the observed value exceed the value the line predicts?
questions.solution: At $x = 14$ the line predicts $y = -3.5(14) + 92$. Since $-3.5(14) = -49$, the prediction is $-49 + 92 = 43$. The observed value is $50$, so it exceeds the prediction by $50 - 43 = 7$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 2x + 11$. Two of the data points are $(5, 25)$ and $(9, 27)$. Which point lies further from the line vertically, and by how much?
questions.solution: At $x = 5$ the line gives $2(5) + 11 = 21$, and $25 - 21 = 4$. At $x = 9$ it gives $2(9) + 11 = 29$, and $27 - 29 = -2$, a gap of $2$. Since $4 > 2$, the point $(5,25)$ lies further from the line.

distractors.B: picked the point with the smaller vertical gap
distractors.C: paired the correct point with the other point's gap
distractors.D: paired the wrong point with the larger gap

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: Across thirty countries, chocolate eaten per person is strongly positively associated with the number of science prizes won per person. A writer claims that eating chocolate improves scientific thinking. What is the strongest objection?
choices: The association described is too weak to discuss.
Thirty countries is a sample, so no pattern found can be real.
The line of best fit for this data would have a negative slope.
Wealthier countries tend to have both higher chocolate consumption and more research funding, so a third variable may explain the pattern.
questions.solution: A country's wealth plausibly raises both figures at once. When a third variable can produce the association, the data gives no support for one quantity causing the other, however strong the association looks.

distractors.A: contradicted the stated strength of the association
distractors.B: rejected all sampling instead of naming a variable affecting both
distractors.C: misstated the direction of the association

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(4, 31)$ and $(12, 55)$. What value does the line predict when $x = 0$?
questions.solution: The slope is $\dfrac{55-31}{12-4} = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3$. Going from $(4, 31)$ back to $x = 0$ moves $4$ units left, lowering $y$ by $4(3) = 12$, so the predicted value is $31 - 12 = 19$.

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: At $x = 0$, $1$, $2$ and $3$ the values of $y$ are $80$, $60$, $45$ and $33.75$. Which model fits this pattern best?
choices: Linear, decreasing by 20 at each step.
Exponential, multiplied by 0.75 at each step.
Linear, decreasing by about 15 at each step.
Exponential, multiplied by 1.25 at each step.
questions.solution: The differences are $-20$, $-15$ and $-11.25$, which are not constant, so the pattern is not linear. The ratios are $\dfrac{60}{80} = 0.75$, $\dfrac{45}{60} = 0.75$ and $\dfrac{33.75}{45} = 0.75$. A constant ratio means an exponential model with factor $0.75$.

distractors.A: used only the first drop of 20 and assumed the differences stay constant
distractors.C: averaged the drops into a single constant difference
distractors.D: used the reciprocal-style factor 1.25 and described growth rather than decay

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 1.1x + 4$, where $x$ is a runner's weekly training distance in miles and $y$ is a fitness score. The data covers distances from $10$ to $60$ miles. Which statement is correct?
choices: The model gives a score of 4 at 0 miles, but 0 lies outside the data range, so that prediction is not supported.
The model gives a score of 4 for a runner who trains 1 mile per week.
The number 4 is the increase in score for each extra mile trained.
The model cannot be used to predict a score for any distance.
questions.solution: Setting $x = 0$ gives $y = 4$, so $4$ is the model's value at zero training. But the data runs only from $10$ to $60$ miles, so $x = 0$ is extrapolation and the value carries no support. Predictions between $10$ and $60$ miles remain reasonable.

distractors.B: evaluated the model at x = 1 instead of x = 0
distractors.C: read the constant term as the slope
distractors.D: ruled out every prediction instead of only those outside the data range

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 0.8x + 6$, where $x$ is the number of advertisements shown and $y$ is sales in thousands of dollars. A manager says, "Each extra thousand dollars of sales requires 0.8 more advertisements." What is wrong with this?
choices: Nothing is wrong with the statement.
The slope gives the change in sales per advertisement: one extra advertisement predicts 0.8 thousand dollars more in sales.
The slope is negative, so sales fall as advertisements rise.
questions.solution: The slope is the change in $y$ for a one-unit rise in $x$, and here $x$ counts advertisements while $y$ measures sales. So $0.8$ means thousands of dollars per advertisement, not advertisements per thousand dollars. The manager reversed the two variables.

distractors.A: accepted the reversed reading of the slope
distractors.B: read the constant term as the slope
distractors.D: misread the sign of a positive slope

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: A programme is modelled by $y = -2.5x + 68$, where $x$ is the number of weeks since it began and $y$ is the number of participants. In which week does the model first predict fewer than $30$ participants?
questions.solution: Solve $-2.5x + 68 < 30$. Subtracting $68$ gives $-2.5x < -38$, and dividing by $-2.5$ reverses the inequality: $x > 15.2$. The first whole week beyond $15.2$ is week $16$.

distractors.A: ignored the constant 68 and solved 2.5x = 30
distractors.B: rounded 15.2 down to 15 instead of up
distractors.D: added instead of subtracting, solving 2.5x = 68 + 30

questions.topicTitle: Scatterplots and models of best fit
questions.stem: Two models are proposed for the same data. Model A is the line $y = 4x + 30$ and model B is the line $y = 6x + 10$. For what value of $x$ do the two models predict the same value of $y$?
questions.solution: Set the two predictions equal: $4x + 30 = 6x + 10$. Subtracting $4x$ from both sides gives $30 = 2x + 10$, then subtracting $10$ gives $2x = 20$, so $x = 10$.

questions.stem: A jar contains 7 green marbles and 13 yellow marbles and nothing else. One marble is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is green?
questions.solution: There are $7+13=20$ marbles in all, and 7 of them are green. A probability is the number of favourable outcomes over the total number of outcomes, so the probability is $\dfrac{7}{20}$.

distractors.B: divided the green marbles by the yellow marbles instead of by the total of 20
distractors.C: found the probability of yellow
distractors.D: wrote the total over the favourable count, inverting the fraction

questions.stem: A class has 30 students, and 12 of them play an instrument. One student is chosen at random. What is the probability, as a decimal, that the student plays an instrument?
questions.solution: The favourable count is 12 and the total is 30, so the probability is $\dfrac{12}{30}=\dfrac{2}{5}$. As a decimal, $2\div 5=0.4$.

distractors.A: gave only the seniors who walk and left out the seniors who cycle

questions.stem: A librarian wants to estimate the proportion of the town's $5000$ library members who read e-books. Which method produces a random sample of the members?

Choosing $50$ members at random from the full list of members
Asking $50$ members of the library's e-book club
Posting the question online and using the first $50$ replies
questions.solution: A random sample has to give every member of the population the same chance of being chosen. Selecting $50$ members at random from the complete membership list does that. People leaving a gym are not representative of all adults in the city
Exercise habits change from week to week
